name: 1X World Model Dataset
field_sources: license=HF dataset card metadata (cardData.license = cc-by-nc-sa-4.0): https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/1x-technologies/world_model_raw_data and README.md front matter; raw_format=Dataset consists of video_{shard}.mp4 + segment_idx_{shard}.bin + states_{shard}.bin + metadata JSON (custom binary/video layout, not RLDS/HDF5/LeRobot/etc): README.md and unpack_data_train_val.py in the HF repo; release_type=Fixed set of 100 train shards + 1 val shard + 250-sample test set, no generation framework/sim platform: HF repo file listing (train_v2.0_raw, val_v2.0_raw, test_v2.0); collection_method=1X blog: 'A human operator can control a fleet of EVEs, tap into their cameras and control their movement to take action from a distance.' https://web.archive.org/web/20241204001902/https://www.1x.tech/eve ; corroborated by 1X World Model blog post describing data gathered from 'operating EVE' https://www.1x.tech/discover/1x-world-model; is_multi_embodiment=All data collected on 1X EVE humanoid only, per 1X World Model blog post and dataset README (no other robot mentioned); embodiment_class=1X World Model blog post: 'thousands of hours of data on EVE humanoids doing diverse mobile manipulation tasks' https://www.1x.tech/discover/1x-world-model; robot_platform=EVE is a 1X Technologies humanoid, not present in RobotPlatform enum; see suggested_new_enum_values; num_arms=State vector index-to-state mapping lists LEFT_SHOULDER_* / LEFT_ELBOW_* / LEFT_WRIST_* and RIGHT_SHOULDER_* / RIGHT_ELBOW_* / RIGHT_WRIST_* (dual arm): README.md Index-to-State Mapping table; dof_per_arm=Each arm has SHOULDER_PITCH/ROLL/YAW (3) + ELBOW_PITCH/YAW (2) + WRIST_PITCH/ROLL (2) = 7 joint values in the state vector: README.md Index-to-State Mapping table (indices 6-12 left, 13-19 right); gripper_type=State vector includes only a binary 'hand closure state (0=open,1=closed)' per hand; exact gripper/hand hardware type (parallel jaw vs dexterous) not confirmed from available sources, hence unknown; hand_pose_representation=State vector encodes hand state as a single binary open/closed flag per hand, not MANO/3D keypoints/joint angles: README.md Index-to-State Mapping (indices 21, 22); has_mobile_base=State vector includes 'Linear Velocity' and 'Angular Velocity' (base motion) and 1X EVE product page describes 'multi-terrain wheels': README.md Index-to-State Mapping (indices 23,24) and https://web.archive.org/web/20241204001902/https://www.1x.tech/eve; action_space=25-dim state vector combines joint positions (hip/knee/ankle/shoulder/elbow/wrist angles) with base linear/angular velocity -> mixed action space: README.md Index-to-State Mapping table; rotation_representation=State vector is joint-angle based (per-joint pitch/roll/yaw), not a Cartesian end-effector orientation encoding: README.md Index-to-State Mapping table; state_dim=unpack_data_train_val.py: states array shape [25] per frame; README.md Index-to-State Mapping lists indices 0-24; fps=train_v2.0_raw/metadata.json and val_v2.0_raw/metadata.json both report {"hz": 30}; fps_variable=Single constant hz=30 reported for both train and val metadata.json, no variable-rate mention; num_camera_views=Only one video_{shard}.mp4 per shard is defined in README.md and unpack_data_train_val.py (single first-person camera); camera_views=1X World Model blog describes 'first-person observations of the EVE Android' recorded from the robot's own onboard camera: https://github.com/1x-technologies/1xgpt README and https://www.1x.tech/discover/1x-world-model; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=Only a single camera stream (video_{shard}.mp4) exists per shard, no multi-camera rig described; has_camera_calibration=No calibration/intrinsics/extrinsics files present in HF repo file listing (only video/segment_idx/states/metadata); depth_coverage=Only RGB video (video_{shard}.mp4) is provided; no depth files in HF repo file listing; additional_modalities=No force/torque, tactile, audio, or eye-gaze streams found in HF repo file listing (video + segment_idx + states + metadata only); has_language_instruction=No task/language instruction fields in metadata.json or states mapping; challenge framing is pure next-frame video prediction: README.md and GitHub 1xgpt README; urdf_available=1x-technologies GitHub org hosts halodi-robot-models, 'Repository of Halodi robot models in urdf format' (Halodi Robotics = former name of 1X Technologies / EVE): https://github.com/1x-technologies/halodi-robot-models; urdf_source=URDF is published by 1X Technologies' own GitHub org (formerly Halodi), i.e. manufacturer-official, not bundled in the dataset repo itself; expected_size_gb=Computed by summing file sizes for all 913 files (train_v2.0_raw + val_v2.0_raw + test_v2.0) via HF API tree endpoint (paginated): https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/1x-technologies/world_model_raw_data/tree/main?recursive=true&expand=true -> 23,972,490,851 bytes = 23.97 GB; expected_duration_hours=Computed as (train 11,254,161 frames + val 50,300 frames) / 30 hz / 3600 = 104.67 hours; consistent with 1X blog claim of 'over 100 hours of vector-quantized video': train_v2.0_raw/metadata.json, val_v2.0_raw/metadata.json, https://www.1x.tech/discover/1x-world-model; paper_url=No peer-reviewed paper found; using 1X's technical blog post announcing the dataset and challenge as the closest technical writeup: https://www.1x.tech/discover/1x-world-model
suggested_new_enum_values: robot_platform=1x_eve — 1X Technologies EVE humanoid (wheeled mobile base, dual 7-DoF arms, single-DoF-per-hand open/close gripper); not present in current RobotPlatform enum. Refs: https://www.1x.tech/eve , https://github.com/1x-technologies/halodi-robot-models

name: AgiBot Digital World
field_sources: source_url=Re-verified reachable (HF API HTTP 200, id agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld, lastModified 2025-02-27) -- https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld; paper_url=Checked the HF README's own BibTeX citation block (only self-cites the project page, no journal/arXiv entry: howpublished={\url{https://agibot-digitalworld.com/}}), and the linked project page badge. No arXiv/paper describing this specific digital-twin release was found, so left blank to avoid misattributing the separate AgiBot World Colosseo paper (arXiv:2503.06669), which describes the real-world Alpha/Beta release, not this simulation companion -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md; license=README "License and Citation" section: "All the data and code within this repo are under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0" -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md; raw_format=README "Dataset Structure" section: raw data is organized as observations/<task_id>/<episode_uuid>/{depth,video} (PNG depth + per-camera MP4) plus meta_info/<task_id>/<episode_uuid>/{task_info.json,proprio_meta_info.h5,camera_parameter.json} -- a bespoke folder layout, not RLDS/HDF5-only/LeRobot/TFRecord. The repo ships scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py specifically to convert this raw layout into LeRobot v2.0, confirming the raw format itself is not LeRobot -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md; release_type=Repo is a static collection of pre-recorded episode tar archives (meta_info/digitaltwin_0..7.tar, observations/digitaltwin_0..7/<uuid> folders) with no in-repo tooling to generate new episodes on demand -- https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/tree/main?recursive=false; collection_method=README Key Features: "1 million+ steps of enhanced digital twins of long-horizon real-world tasks from AgiBot World" plus "500,000+ steps of atomic tasks automatically generated by agents" -- both halves of the dataset are produced in simulation (digital-twin reconstruction / agent-driven generation), not live teleoperation -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md; secondary_collection_methods=human_to_robot_synthesis: the "digital twins" are simulation reconstructions of real human-teleoperated long-horizon tasks originally captured in AgiBot World (README: "enhanced digital twins of long-horizon real-world tasks from AgiBot World"). scene_asset_curation: sample task_info.json label_info.objects entries reference a curated external 3D object asset bank (e.g. "omni6DPose_toy_motorcycle_023", "omni6DPose_book_000", "genie_storage_box_002"), confirmed by downloading and inspecting task_info.json files extracted via HTTP range requests against sample_dataset.zip's central directory -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md, https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/resolve/main/sample_dataset.zip; is_multi_embodiment=False. All 8 task shards (digitaltwin_0..7) use the same joint-name schema (head/body/arm/effector) in scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py and the same 34-DoF proprioceptive layout documented in the README; no second robot platform is referenced anywhere -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py; embodiment_class=Kept consistent with the sibling agibot_world / agibot_world_2026 registry entries (same AgiBot platform family), which classify it as dual_arm (mobility captured separately via has_mobile_base) rather than humanoid -- configs/agibot_world.yaml, configs/agibot_world_2026.yaml; robot_platform=README terminology section: 34 total joint DoF = 2 head + 2 waist + 7-per-arm x2 + gripper-per-hand x2, matching the AGIBOT G1 platform used for the original AgiBot World Alpha/Beta release (whose real-world long-horizon tasks this dataset digital-twins). This dataset predates (Feb 2025) and is architecturally distinct from the newer AGIBOT G2 platform used by the 2026 agibot_world_2026 release -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md; num_arms=README proprioceptive schema: /state/end/position and /state/end/orientation have shape [N, 2, ...] documented as "left [:, 0], right [:, 1]"; convert_to_lerobot.py arm_joint_names lists 7 joints x2 suffixed _l/_r -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md, https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py; dof_per_arm=scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py arm_joint_names: Joint1_l/r through Joint7_l/r -- exactly 7 joints per arm -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py; dof_per_hand=scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py effector_joint_names lists exactly 2 joints per hand (e.g. left_Left_1_Joint, left_Right_1_Joint). This is the figure actually used to build the released state/action vectors, so it is trusted over the README's generic terminology-section prose ("8 Dof each gripper"), which appears to describe a different/fuller hardware DOF budget not exposed in this dataset's recorded data -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py (used value); https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md (conflicting prose, not used); gripper_type=Revised from an initial "dexterous_hand" guess after finding concrete evidence: effector_joint_names in convert_to_lerobot.py names exactly 2 opposing joints per hand (*_Left_1_Joint, *_Right_1_Joint), matching a 2-actuator parallel-jaw-style gripper rather than a multi-fingered dexterous hand -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py; hand_pose_representation=Left as none -- the effector state/action is a single aggregate open-range value per hand (2 joint positions, not per-finger keypoints/MANO/joint-angle hand-shape encoding) -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py; has_mobile_base=True. README proprioceptive schema documents /state/robot/position (xyz, "z is always 0 in meters") and /action/robot/velocity ("vel along x axis, yaw rate") -- i.e. a wheeled/planar mobile base with velocity control, independent of the simplified 22-dim LeRobot conversion which omits base state -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md; action_space=scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py builds the released "action" feature (shape [22]) purely from head/body/arm/effector JOINT POSITION arrays (state_joint indexed by joint name) -- no end-effector pose or base velocity is included in this canonical action vector -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py; action_frame=scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py computes action arrays explicitly as consecutive-frame differences: "action_arm = state_arm[1:] - state_arm[:-1]" (same pattern for head/body/effector), i.e. delta joint positions between frames -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py; rotation_representation=Left as none for the canonical released state/action (hstack of head+body+arm+effector joint positions only) -- no wrist/end-effector orientation component (quaternion etc.) is part of the 22-dim state or action vectors actually produced by the conversion script, even though the raw h5 separately stores /state/end/orientation as wxyz quaternions (unused by this conversion) -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py; state_dim=scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py LeRobot feature dict: "observation.state": {"shape": [22]} -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py; action_dim=scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py LeRobot feature dict: "action": {"shape": [22]} -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py; fps=scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py: every video feature declares "video.fps": 30.0, and process_video() re-encodes with ffmpeg "-r 30"; visualize call also uses fps=30 -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py; fps_variable=False -- fps is declared as a fixed 30.0 for every one of the 8 documented camera video streams, with no per-episode/per-camera variation noted -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py; num_camera_views=Confirmed two independent ways: (1) scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py LeRobot feature dict lists 8 distinct video keys (top_head, hand_left, hand_right, head_center_fisheye, head_left_fisheye, head_right_fisheye, back_left_fisheye, back_right_fisheye) plus 1 depth-only key (cam_top_depth, same physical camera as top_head); (2) sample_dataset.zip video/ folder contains 8 distinct *.mp4 basenames (head, hand_left, hand_right, head_front_fisheye, head_left_fisheye, head_right_fisheye, back_left_fisheye, back_right_fisheye) -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py, https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/resolve/main/sample_dataset.zip; camera_views=Mapped from the 8 raw camera names: head/head_front_fisheye/head_left_fisheye/head_right_fisheye -> head; hand_left -> left_wrist; hand_right -> right_wrist; back_left_fisheye/back_right_fisheye (rear-facing, no matching enum category) -> other -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/resolve/main/sample_dataset.zip; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=True -- scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py assembles all 8 camera video keys plus depth into a single per-frame LeRobot record keyed by the same frame index, i.e. rendered/captured in lockstep by construction of the simulator -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/scripts/convert_to_lerobot.py; has_camera_calibration=True -- README documents a per-episode camera_parameter.json containing "all cameras' intrinsic and extrinsic parameters" -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md; depth_coverage=Partial -- directly confirmed by inspecting sample_dataset.zip: the depth/<frame>/ folders contain exactly 3 PNGs (head.png, hand_left.png, hand_right.png) out of the 8 total documented camera views, so depth is available for head + both wrist cameras only, not the 4 fisheye or 2 back cameras -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/resolve/main/sample_dataset.zip; additional_modalities=Checked, left empty. No mention of force/torque, tactile, audio, or eye-gaze sensing in the README or conversion scripts; the h5 wrench/effort fields are explicitly marked "Not available for now" -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md; has_language_instruction=True -- README states each action_config slice in task_info.json "includes a start and end time, the corresponding atomic skill, and the language instruction"; sample task_info.json files (fetched via range requests) show action_text/skill fields per action slice, though the specific sampled example instances have empty-string text values -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md; num_task_types=Directly confirmed by fetching and decompressing all 8 task_info.json files bundled in sample_dataset.zip (one per task shard, via HTTP range requests against the zip's central directory): digitaltwin_0..7 map 1:1 to 8 distinct task_name values -- place_trash_into_ground_dustbin, place_objects_into_drawer, insert_pen, place_objects_into_handbag, pick_fruits_from_basket_into_dish, pick_toys_into_box, pick_fruits_place_dish, place_trash_into_table_dustbin_dual_arm -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/resolve/main/sample_dataset.zip; urdf_available=Checked HF README and repo file tree; no URDF file or link is provided in this dataset repo. Left blank rather than guessing at an external AgiBot-World GitHub URDF, since a GitHub API rate limit prevented verification -- https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/tree/main?recursive=false; urdf_source=Left blank -- see urdf_available.; expected_size_gb=HF API dataset info usedStorage field: 7,635,467,064,099 bytes = 7635.47 GB -- https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld?expand[]=usedStorage; expected_num_episodes=Directly counted by paginating the HF tree API (recursive=false, following Link: rel="next" cursors) over each of the 8 observations/digitaltwin_N folders and summing episode-uuid subfolder counts: 7794 + 8876 + 8842 + 6380 + 6943 + 9968 + 78 + 103 = 48984 episodes total. Note: this measured total implies a much higher steps/episode ratio than a naive read of the README's headline "1M+ / 500K+ steps" figures would suggest, so that headline may reflect an earlier/partial snapshot rather than the currently fully-published corpus -- flagged for human awareness -- https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/tree/main/observations/digitaltwin_0?recursive=false (and digitaltwin_1..7 analogously); expected_duration_hours=Checked, left blank. No total duration/hours figure is stated on the card or README, and computing it would require decoding every episode video (not attempted) -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md; num_subjects=Checked, left blank. This dataset's own collection process is simulation (digital-twin reconstruction / agent-generated atomic tasks), not live human teleoperation, so a "subject count" for this release specifically is not documented and not clearly applicable -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md; num_scenes=README Key Features: "5 classes of scenes" (exact, not a lower bound) -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md; num_objects=README Key Features: "180+ classes of objects" -- recorded as 180; note the source states this as a lower bound ("180+"), not a precise exact count -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotDigitalWorld/raw/main/README.md

name: AgiBot-World
field_sources: source_url=Re-verified reachable (HTTP 200 via HF datasets API); card id/pretty_name 'AgiBot World 2026' matches the stub's recorded name/id -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026; paper_url=Searched arXiv (export.arxiv.org query all:"AgiBot World"), the official OpenDriveLab/AgiBot-World GitHub README, and the HF README's own citation block. No paper describing this specific G2-based/29-task/2026 release was found -- the HF README's BibTeX only self-cites the dataset page (no journal/arXiv entry). The original project paper, arXiv:2503.06669 ('AgiBot World Colosseo'), describes the earlier AGIBOT G1-based Alpha/Beta release (217 tasks, 1M+ trajectories) and does not describe this dataset, so it was deliberately NOT attached here to avoid misattribution -- left blank -- https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.06669 (checked and rejected), https://github.com/OpenDriveLab/AgiBot-World (checked, does not list AgiBotWorld2026); license=Re-derived from HF cardData ('license: cc-by-nc-sa-4.0') and README 'License and Citation' section ('CC BY-NC-SA 4.0'). CORRECTED from the prior pass: the schema's LicenseEnum now includes CC_BY_NC_SA_4_0 = "CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0" (this enum value did not exist, or was believed not to exist, at the time of the earlier onboarding pass, which left license blank and filed it under suggested_new_enum_values instead) -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026/raw/main/README.md; raw_format=Re-confirmed via HF README.md 'Dataset Structure' section: 'LeRobot version reference: v2.1' -- data stored as meta/ (jsonl+json), data/ (Apache Parquet per episode), videos/ (MP4 per camera per episode) -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026/raw/main/README.md; release_type=Re-confirmed fixed_episode_dataset -- the repo is a static collection of pre-recorded episode archives (tar.gz per task, real-world + simulation) with no code/tooling in-repo to generate new episodes on demand; not a generation_framework, scene_platform, or rl_benchmark_env -- https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026/tree/main?recursive=true; collection_method=Re-confirmed via HF README.md Overview: 'Collected on the AGIBOT G2 robot platform through a free-form collection mode'; Annotation Layers section documents 'take_over' and 'Intervention Frame' fields indicating supervised/corrected teleoperation -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026/raw/main/README.md; secondary_collection_methods=Newly filled. The HF tree API (recursive) shows a top-level `simulation/` directory (6 task types x g2_swift_picker/lite + lite_depth_patch variants) sitting alongside the real-world `ImitationLearning/` and `RichInteraction/` directories within the same dataset repo, and the README states simulation data (via digital-twin 1:1 scenario reconstruction) is included alongside the real-world data -- https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026/tree/main?recursive=true; is_multi_embodiment=Newly filled (false). README Overview states data was 'Collected on the AGIBOT G2 robot platform' (singular), and every simulation task subfolder is namespaced under a single embodiment id (`g2_swift_picker`); no second robot platform is referenced anywhere in the card or README -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026/raw/main/README.md; embodiment_class=Re-confirmed. HF dataset card tags include 'dual-arm' -- https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026 (cardData.tags); num_arms=Re-confirmed. Same 'dual-arm' tag, plus README schema example keys state/left_effector/position and state/right_effector/position confirming two arms -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026/raw/main/README.md; has_mobile_base=Newly filled (true), with lower confidence than the directly-cited fields above -- inferred from two indirect sources: (1) this dataset's own README Instruction-Segments example lists 'Bend waist forward' as a primitive skill, implying a torso/waist joint typical of mobile humanoid-style bases; (2) the official OpenDriveLab/AgiBot-World GitHub README's Key Features section describes the AGIBOT platform family generically as 'mobile dual-arm robots'. Neither source is a direct, dataset-specific confirmation for the G2 platform, so this is flagged as an inference, not a hard fact -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026/raw/main/README.md (waist skill example), https://github.com/OpenDriveLab/AgiBot-World (Key Features section); action_space=Re-confirmed. README.md 'State and Action Vectors' example keys: action/joint/position and action/robot/velocity -- i.e. joint-position control for arms plus a separate velocity command channel (likely base/whole-body), which does not map to a single pure action_space value -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026/raw/main/README.md; num_camera_views=Re-confirmed. README.md 'Camera Feature Keys' section lists 9 observation.images.* keys: top_head, hand_left, hand_right, head_depth, head_left_fisheye, head_right_fisheye, head_back_fisheye_color, head_stereo_left_color, head_stereo_right_color -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026/raw/main/README.md; camera_views=Re-confirmed. Same camera key list mapped to semantic categories: top_head/head_depth/head_*fisheye*/head_stereo_* -> head; hand_left -> left_wrist; hand_right -> right_wrist -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026/raw/main/README.md; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=Newly filled (true). field_sources: license=GitHub LICENSE file (MIT), https://github.com/askforalfred/alfred/blob/master/LICENSE; paper_url=arXiv:1912.01734, ALFRED: A Benchmark for Interpreting Grounded Instructions for Everyday Tasks (CVPR 2020); raw_format=Dataset shipped as trajectory JSON + PNG/JPEG images + video.mp4 + PDDL problem files + ResNet feature tensors (feat_conv.pt); no single standard format applies. https://github.com/askforalfred/alfred/blob/master/data/README.md; release_type=Fixed benchmark of 8,055 pre-generated expert demonstrations with official train/val-seen/val-unseen/test splits used for the ALFRED leaderboard. https://askforalfred.com; collection_method=Expert demonstrations produced by a PDDL symbolic planner executed inside the AI2-THOR simulator (not human teleoperation). arXiv:1912.01734 Sec 3 ('Planner-based expert demonstrations'); is_multi_embodiment=All demonstrations use the single default AI2-THOR embodied agent. arXiv:1912.01734; embodiment_class=AI2-THOR agent has a mobile base (navigation) and interacts with/picks up/places objects; closest existing enum fit is mobile_manipulator, though ALFRED has no explicit simulated arm -- interaction is an abstract inventory operation guided by a predicted pixel mask, not arm kinematics. See suggested_new_enum_values. arXiv:1912.01734 Sec 3; gripper_type=No physical gripper is simulated; Pickup/Put are abstract inventory operations targeted by a predicted interaction mask, closest existing fit is 'none'. arXiv:1912.01734 Sec 3; hand_pose_representation=No hand/finger pose is modeled or published for this benchmark. arXiv:1912.01734; has_mobile_base=Agent navigates the scene via 5 navigation actions (MoveAhead, RotateRight, RotateLeft, LookUp, LookDown). arXiv:1912.01734 Sec 3; rotation_representation=Agent orientation changes are fixed discrete increments (RotateLeft/Right, LookUp/Down); there is no continuous wrist/eef rotation representation since no end-effector is modeled. arXiv:1912.01734 Sec 3; num_camera_views=Single egocentric RGB camera at the agent's viewpoint ('egocentric vision'). arXiv:1912.01734 Abstract, Sec 3; camera_views=Egocentric first-person camera mounted at the agent's own viewpoint; closest enum fit is 'head'. arXiv:1912.01734 Abstract; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=Only one camera view is used throughout. arXiv:1912.01734 Sec 3; depth_coverage='Currently, the dataset only provides 300x300 RGB images' -- depth/instance-segmentation frames are only obtainable if a user separately re-runs the augment_trajectories.py augmentation script; not part of the released dataset itself. https://github.com/askforalfred/alfred/blob/master/gen/README.md; has_language_instruction='ALFRED includes 25,743 English language directives describing 8,055 expert demonstrations' (high-level goal + step-by-step instructions). arXiv:1912.01734 Abstract; num_task_types='We introduce 7 different task types parameterized by 84 object classes in 120 scenes.' arXiv:1912.01734 Sec 3; urdf_available=No physical robot; AI2-THOR virtual agent has no published URDF.; urdf_source=Not applicable -- no URDF exists for the AI2-THOR virtual agent used in ALFRED.; expected_size_gb=GitHub data/README.md: 'Full Dataset (~109GB): Trajectory JSONs, Raw Images, PDDL States, Videos, Full Resnet Features' (smaller 'Modeling Quickstart' ~17GB and 'Lite' 35MB download options also exist). https://github.com/askforalfred/alfred/blob/master/data/README.md; expected_num_episodes='25,743 English language directives describing 8,055 expert demonstrations averaging 50 steps each, resulting in 428,322 image-action pairs.' arXiv:1912.01734 Abstract; num_scenes='120 indoor scenes in AI2-THOR 2.0' (arXiv:1912.01734 Sec 3); confirmed by gen/constants.py: 24 kitchens + 24 living rooms + 24 bedrooms + 24 bathrooms (train) + 6 each (test) = 120. https://github.com/askforalfred/alfred/blob/master/gen/constants.py; num_objects='ALFRED contains expert demonstrations of these seven tasks executed using combinations of 58 unique object classes and 26 receptacle object classes' (58+26=84, matching the abstract's '84 object classes'). arXiv:1912.01734 Sec 3
suggested_new_enum_values: action_space=ALFRED's action space is 13 discrete symbolic actions (5 navigation: MoveAhead, RotateRight, RotateLeft, LookUp, LookDown; 7 interaction: Pickup, Put, Open, Close, ToggleOn, ToggleOff, Slice -- interaction actions targeted via a predicted pixel mask, plus a Stop action), not a continuous joint/eef control space. None of joint_position/joint_velocity/joint_torque/eef_pose/mixed fit; recommend adding a 'discrete_symbolic' ActionSpace value for AI2-THOR-style simulation benchmarks (ALFRED, RoboTHOR, ProcTHOR, etc).arXiv:1912.01734 Sec 3; robot_platform=No RobotPlatform enum value represents a purely virtual/simulated agent with no physical hardware counterpart (e.g. the default AI2-THOR agent used in ALFRED). Recommend adding a value such as 'ai2thor_virtual_agent' or a generic 'simulated_virtual_agent'.; embodiment_class=mobile_manipulator is the closest existing fit, but ALFRED's AI2-THOR agent has no explicit simulated arm/gripper kinematics -- interaction is an abstract inventory operation guided by a 2D pixel mask, not arm motion. A dedicated 'virtual_embodied_agent' (or similar) EmbodimentClass value would better distinguish AI2-THOR/ALFRED-style benchmarks from real mobile-manipulator robots.

name: ALOHA Unleashed
field_sources: source_url=Re-verified 2026-07-10 via curl: https://aloha-unleashed.github.io/ is still live and is the official Google DeepMind project page (author list: Tony Z. Confirmed live at https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13126 and PDF fetched directly for this re-verification pass.; license=No public dataset release found as of this re-check (2026-07-10, ~21 months after the Oct 2024 paper). No license is attached to any downloadable data because none is published.; release_type=Paper describes collection of a fixed count of demonstrations (26,241 real + several thousand simulated) for a closed set of 8 tasks, not a generative/procedural environment or a standing RL benchmark suite -- conceptually a fixed_episode_dataset methodology even though no matching data blob has actually been published (see license note above).; collection_method=Paper Sec 3.2 'Data Collection': 'ALOHA allows bimanual teleoperation via a puppeteering interface, which allows a human teleoperator to backdrive two smaller leader arms, whose joints are synchronized with two larger follower arms.' Re-confirmed by re-reading full PDF text on 2026-07-10.; secondary_collection_methods=Paper Sec 4.3 'Simulation experiments': 'We teleoperate the simulated environments... using the MuJoCo Menagerie [53][54] model from ALOHA 2... to collect human demonstrations for each task' for the 3 simulated tasks (SingleInsertion: 522 demos, DoubleInsertion: 201 demos, MugOnPlate: 550 demos per Table 3). This is still teleoperation in mechanism, but the platform is a simulated (not physical) embodiment, so it is logged as a secondary collection method distinct from the primary real-robot teleop.; embodiment_class=Paper Sec 3 / project page and ALOHA 2 hardware report (arXiv:2405.02292, p.2): 'ALOHA 2 ... consists of a bimanual parallel-jaw gripper workcell with two ViperX 6-DoF arms.'; robot_platform=Paper Sec 3.1: 'The policy outputs 12 absolute joint positions, 6 for each 6-dof ViperX arm.' ALOHA 2 follower arms are Trossen/Interbotix ViperX 300 6-DoF (confirmed via ALOHA 2 hardware report arXiv:2405.02292 p.2: 'two ViperX 6-DoF arms (the follower), along with 2 smaller WidowX arms (the leader)'; the action/state space is built from the follower ViperX arms). Also cross-checked via MuJoCo Menagerie ALOHA 2 model, derived from trossen_vx300s.; is_multi_embodiment=No evidence of any embodiment other than the ALOHA 2 dual-ViperX-arm workcell (real) / its MuJoCo Menagerie mirror (sim) anywhere in the paper; all 8 tasks (5 real + 3 sim) use the same platform.; num_arms=Paper Sec 3: 'two 6-DoF arms' (bimanual workcell). Re-confirmed.; dof_per_arm=Paper Sec 3.1: '6-dof ViperX arm.' Re-confirmed.; gripper_type=Paper Sec 3 / project page: 'bimanual parallel-jaw gripper workcell.' Re-confirmed; also matches ALOHA 2 hardware report's "Leader/Follower Grippers" sections which only describe parallel-jaw finger designs.; hand_pose_representation=Not applicable / none: gripper_type is parallel_jaw (simple 2-finger gripper actuated by a single continuous open/close value per arm), not a dexterous multi-finger hand, so no MANO/keypoints/joint-angle hand-shape encoding is used anywhere in the paper.; has_mobile_base=Paper and ALOHA 2 hardware report both describe ALOHA 2 as a stationary 'workcell' mounted on a 48x30" table with a fixed aluminum frame; no mobile base component is mentioned anywhere (contrast with 'Mobile ALOHA', a different, unrelated system).; action_space=Paper Sec 3.1: 'The policy outputs 12 absolute joint positions, 6 for each 6-dof ViperX arm, and a continuous value for gripper position for each of the two grippers.' Re-confirmed.; action_frame=Paper Sec 3.1: 'The policy outputs 12 absolute joint positions...' Re-confirmed.; rotation_representation=Action/state space is pure joint-space (14-dim joint positions + gripper), no Cartesian/orientation representation is used; paper Sec 3.1. Re-confirmed.; state_dim=CORRECTED reasoning (value unchanged at 14): the paper does not directly state a raw proprioceptive vector length in numerals. Sec 3.1 says the proprioceptive state 'consists of the joint positions and gripper values for each of the arms' and that after projection it contributes 1 of 'a total of 1201 latent feature dimensions' (1200 image-patch tokens + 1 proprioception token) -- that 1201 figure describes transformer *token* count, not the raw state dimensionality, and the prior field_sources entry conflated the two. state_dim=14 is inferred by symmetry with the explicitly-stated 14-dim action tensor (6 joints + 1 gripper value per arm x 2 arms), matching the standard ALOHA/ACT proprioception convention, but is not itself a directly-quoted number in this paper -- flagged as a soft inference for human review.; action_dim=Paper Sec 3.1: 'policy outputs a tensor of shape (50, 14)' i.e. 14-dim action per timestep (12 joint positions + 2 gripper values). Re-confirmed.; fps=Paper Sec 3.1: 'we are able to surpass our target frequency of 50Hz'; action chunk of 50 actions = 'a trajectory spanning 1 second' implies 50Hz nominal control/recording rate. Also directly confirmed in ALOHA 2 hardware report (arXiv:2405.02292) Sec 'Teleoperation': 'We record leader and follower joint data at 50Hz.'; fps_variable=Inferred from paper Sec 3.1 and ALOHA 2 hardware report: system is described around a fixed 50Hz target/logging rate, not a variable-rate recording scheme.; num_camera_views=Paper Sec 3.1: 'multimodal inputs (4 images from different viewpoints...)' and 'Each of the 4 RGB images is resized to 480x640x3...'. This is the best fit per arXiv:2410.08464 abstract/Sec II-III: a portable AR-headset + Rokoko haptic data-glove system with no physical robot present during collection, which retargets human hand/wrist motion to a virtual robot via real-time IK and records the resulting robot-joint-space trajectory directly with live visual/haptic feedback on kinematic feasibility and collisions -- distinct from 'umi' (a handheld mechanical mimic of the actual gripper) and from generic 'human_to_robot_synthesis' (typically post-hoc retargeting from passive human video with no live feedback loop). The suggested_new_enum_values entry from the prior pass is removed since the value now exists natively in the schema.; secondary_collection_methods=No evidence of a second, distinct collection mechanism blended into this dataset -- all 5 released hdf5 files use the same AR-headset + haptic-glove IK-retargeting pipeline (arXiv:2410.08464 Sec III), unlike e.g. ALOHA Unleashed which mixes real teleop with simulated teleop. Left empty.; is_multi_embodiment=true (new field, filled): arXiv:2410.08464 explicitly frames this as cross-embodiment data collection -- Fig. 3 caption "Cross-Embodiment Data Collection", Sec III-A bullet "Cross-embodiment. Unchanged.; dof_per_arm=Re-verified 2026-07-10 -- Franka Panda is a standard 7-DOF arm (robot_platform identity); still not restated as an explicit numeral in the paper text found. Cross-checked against ARCap's own Sec III-A: "each finger of the leap hand has one redundant degree of freedom," consistent with 4 DOF/finger. Applies to the 4 of 5 released hdf5 files that use the dexterous hand (clutter/clutter_users/open_bottle/wild); the assemble (Fin-ray parallel-jaw) file has only a 1-DOF open/close gripper, not a comparable per-hand DOF count -- 16 is chosen as the dominant value, matching the existing gripper_type reasoning below.; gripper_type=Re-verified 2026-07-10: arXiv:2410.08464 Sec III-A: two interchangeable end-effectors -- 'Leap Hand, a fully actuated, four-finger dexterous hand' and 'the Fin-ray gripper, a compliant parallel-jaw-like gripper'. The majority of released HF files (clutter, clutter_users, open_bottle, wild) correspond to dexterous-hand tasks per the paper's task descriptions, while 'assemble' (Lego) uses the Fin-ray parallel-jaw gripper -- dexterous_hand chosen as dominant value; dataset actually spans both gripper types across task files. Unchanged.; hand_pose_representation=joint_angles (new field, filled): arXiv:2410.08464 Sec III-B lists recorded data as including "Joint angle for the virtual robot solved by IK," and Sec III-B-2 states the policy action "for dex hand, consists of the target joint angles of each finger." This is the finger/hand-shape encoding actually persisted in the dexterous-hand task files -- distinct from the Rokoko data-glove fingertip positions used only as an intermediate IK target for the *human* hand during retargeting (Sec III-A: "the data gloves capture fingertip positions relative to the wrist"), which are not what is stored as the dataset's hand-pose representation. Applies to the dominant dexterous-hand files, consistent with the gripper_type/dof_per_hand reasoning above; the assemble (parallel-jaw) file has no dexterous hand-shape encoding (binary open/close only).; has_mobile_base=Re-verified 2026-07-10 -- no mention of a mobile base anywhere in the paper, GitHub repo, or HF card; system is a fixed-base Franka Panda arm setup. field_sources: source_url=https://github.com/NVlabs/dexmimicgen README.md: "Website: https://dexmimicgen.github.io" -- re-verified 2026-07-10 by re-fetching the GitHub README directly; stub source_url confirmed correct, no change needed.; paper_url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.24185 -- ICRA 2025 paper "DexMimicGen: Automated Data Generation for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation via Imitation Learning"; confirmed via both the GitHub README ("Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.24185") and the arXiv abstract page itself. New field, filled 2026-07-10.; license=CORRECTED from CC-BY-4.0 to CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0. The GitHub README (https://github.com/NVlabs/dexmimicgen#license) states "the datasets are released under CC-BY 4.0", but this is contradicted by the actual license shipped with the released data itself: the Hugging Face dataset repo https://huggingface.co/datasets/MimicGen/dexmimicgen_datasets README.md frontmatter declares "license: cc-by-nc-sa-4.0" (confirmed via HF API cardData.license = "cc-by-nc-sa-4.0"), and the repo's own LICENSE file (https://huggingface.co/datasets/MimicGen/dexmimicgen_datasets/raw/main/LICENSE) is an "NVIDIA License" whose Sec. 3.3 Use Limitation states the Work "only may be used or intended for use non-commercially... for research or evaluation purposes only". We generate 21K demos across these tasks from just 60 source human demos." Only 60 of the ~21,060 total demos (~0.3%) are genuine human teleoperation (collected via an iPhone/RoboTurk interface for parallel-jaw tasks and an Apple Vision Pro + OmniH2O retargeting system for dexterous-hand/humanoid tasks, per Sec. V "Teleoperation System"); the remaining ~99.7% are algorithmically synthesized via object-centric segmentation + transformation + replay in physics simulation (Sec. IV), the same MimicGen-family technique already classified as human_to_robot_synthesis in configs/mimicgen.yaml for consistency (that entry: "only 120 of ~50,120 demos are human teleop... matching the 'human_to_robot_synthesis' semantics"). V "System Design": "We focus on three embodiments: (1) bimanual Panda arms equipped with parallel-jaw grippers, (2) bimanual Panda arms with dexterous hands, and (3) a GR-1 humanoid equipped with dexterous hands." Also confirmed via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVlabs/dexmimicgen/main/environments.md, which lists the 9 environments with their "suggested embodiments" split 3/3/3 across exactly these three embodiments.; embodiment_class=New field, filled dual_arm (majority-of-tasks representative, following the same convention as configs/humanoidbench.yaml / configs/yubi.yaml for is_multi_embodiment=true entries). 6 of 9 task environments (TwoArmThreading, TwoArmThreePieceAssembly, TwoArmTransport, TwoArmDrawerCleanup, TwoArmBoxCleanup, TwoArmLiftTray -- per environments.md) use non-humanoid bimanual Panda arms (dual_arm); the remaining 3 (TwoArmCoffee, TwoArmPouring, TwoArmCanSortRandom) use the GR-1 humanoid embodiment instead. V "System Design": fixed-base bimanual Panda arms and a stationary tabletop GR-1 humanoid setup; no mobile base described in any of the 9 released tasks. III "Prerequisites" (Assumption A1): action consists of an end-effector pose command plus a hand/gripper actuation command (1-D for parallel-jaw, 6-D joint command for dexterous hand). name: EgoAllo
field_sources: source_url=https://egoallo.github.io/ -- re-verified reachable (curl, 2026-07-10); project page for arXiv:2410.03665, links to https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo. Unchanged from prior pass.; paper_url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.03665 -- "Estimating Body and Hand Motion in an Ego-sensed World" (Yi, Ye, Zheng, Li, Muller, Pavlakos, Ma, Malik, Kanazawa, 2024); field was blank in the prior pass, newly filled here; license=https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo/blob/main/LICENSE -- re-fetched raw file directly (curl), confirms MIT License, Copyright (c) 2024 Brent Yi. Note (unchanged from prior pass): the underlying AMASS training data and the Google-Drive-hosted checkpoint/example-trajectories zip are not covered by this code license (README 'Preprocessing Training Data': 'Due to licensing constraints, we cannot redistribute the preprocessed [AMASS] data.'); raw_format=CORRECTED from "Custom" to "VRS": schema.py RawFormat enum now includes an explicit VRS member (was not available/used in the prior onboarding pass, which fell back to Custom). https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo README ('Running inference' section) confirms the released per-sequence data is centered on a Project Aria VRS file ('A VRS file from Project Aria, which contains calibrations and images') plus auxiliary MPS CSV/gz outputs and an optional hamer_outputs.pkl -- VRS is now the closest exact-enum match for the primary raw capture container; the CSV/pkl side files are auxiliary derived outputs, not the primary format; release_type=https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo download_checkpoint_and_data.sh -- ships a fixed, versioned "egoallo_example_trajectories.zip" (8.17GB) of pre-recorded per-sequence captures (VRS + MPS + optional HaMeR outputs), which is a fixed episode-style release rather than a generation_framework/scene_platform/rl_benchmark_env. Caveat carried over from re-verification: EgoAllo is fundamentally a motion-estimation *method* paper (arXiv:2410.03665) whose primary training/eval data are external third-party datasets (AMASS, RICH, Aria Digital Twins, EgoExo4D per paper Section 4 "Evaluation"), not a purpose-collected episode corpus; the example-trajectories package is a small demo/sample release. fixed_episode_dataset is still the best available fit among the 4 enum options and matches this registry's stated batch-migration default (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-registry-schema-refinement-design.md section 4B: "其余55个...→ fixed_episode_dataset"), so left unchanged, but this residual nature-of-release ambiguity is why review_status stays pending_human_review; collection_method=re-verified https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.03665 abstract: "Using only egocentric SLAM poses and images" captured by a human wearing a head-mounted Project Aria device. Unchanged from prior pass.; secondary_collection_methods=re-checked arXiv:2410.03665 full text and https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo README -- no secondary capture pipeline (e.g. teleop, simulation, human-to-robot synthesis) is described; the only capture modality is the single egocentric Aria device. Left empty.; is_multi_embodiment=arXiv:2410.03665 Section 3 ("Method") and https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo -- system is designed around exactly one embodiment (a single human wearer with a head-mounted Project Aria device); no other embodiment type is captured or discussed. Field was blank in the prior pass, newly filled as false.; num_arms=arXiv:2410.03665 -- SMPL-H output includes both left/right hand pose parameters (guided by HaMeR two-hand estimates), i.e. a two-armed human body. Re-confirmed, unchanged.; dof_per_hand=Derived from arXiv:2410.03665 Section 3.1: "local joint rotation matrices Theta^t in R^{51x3x3}" -- per standard SMPL-H convention (Romero et al. 2017 MANO/"Embodied Hands"; SMPL-H = SMPL body + MANO hands), 51 = 21 non-root body joints + 15 hand joints x 2 hands, i.e. 15 joints/hand. Since each joint is parameterized as a full 3x3 rotation matrix (3 rotational DOF, not a 1D flexion hinge), dof_per_hand = 15 x 3 = 45. Field was blank in the prior pass, newly filled; flagged as a computed/derived value rather than a number stated verbatim in the paper.; gripper_type=https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo -- no robot end-effector/gripper hardware is involved at all; captured subject is a human wearing a head-mounted sensor, so 'none' (no gripper) applies rather than any robotic gripper category. Re-confirmed, unchanged.; hand_pose_representation=arXiv:2410.03665 Section 3.2.2: HaMeR intermediate hand observations are explicitly "3D hand estimates in the form of MANO [Romero et al.] joint parameters and camera-centric 3D hand keypoints"; EgoAllo's own output hand pose is the SMPL-H hand component, which is architecturally the MANO hand model embedded in SMPL-H. Field was blank in the prior pass, newly filled as mano.; rotation_representation=re-verified arXiv:2410.03665 Section 3.1 (exact quote): "local joint rotation matrices Theta^t in R^{51x3x3}" -- confirmed unchanged from prior pass.; fps=re-verified https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo README 'Preprocessing Training Data' step 2: AMASS preprocessing script performs "Downsampling to 30fps". Unchanged from prior pass.; fps_variable=re-verified https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo README -- AMASS source mocap sub-datasets have varying native capture rates before being downsampled uniformly to 30fps for training; Aria capture streams (RGB/SLAM/IMU) also run at multiple native rates. Unchanged from prior pass.; num_camera_views=re-verified arXiv:2410.03665 / https://egoallo.github.io/ -- single head-mounted Project Aria device is the capture rig. Unchanged from prior pass.; camera_views=re-verified https://egoallo.github.io/ and README -- described throughout as a 'head-mounted device'; all imagery is egocentric/head-worn, no third-person or wrist cameras. Unchanged from prior pass.; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=No evidence of a synchronized multi-viewpoint rig (e.g. combined third-person + wrist cameras): the only sensor is a single head-mounted Project Aria unit, consistent with num_camera_views=1. Field was blank in the prior pass, newly filled as false.; has_camera_calibration=re-verified https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo README 'Running inference' step 3: "A VRS file from Project Aria, which contains calibrations and images." Unchanged from prior pass.; depth_coverage=re-verified https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo README -- Project Aria MPS outputs include semidense_points.csv.gz, a sparse/semi-dense SLAM point cloud (partial 3D scene structure); there is no dense per-pixel depth sensor on the device. Unchanged from prior pass.; additional_modalities=Checked arXiv:2410.03665 full text and README for eye-gaze/audio/tactile/force-torque mentions -- none found; the paper never discusses using Aria's eye-tracking cameras or microphone array, even though the Aria hardware platform generically includes those sensors. Because the released VRS/MPS package's exact stream contents for these channels are not documented in EgoAllo's own sources, left empty rather than assumed.; has_language_instruction=re-verified arXiv:2410.03665 and https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo -- no language-instruction annotation or task-language pipeline is described anywhere in the paper or repo; this is a motion-estimation system, not a language-conditioned policy dataset. Unchanged from prior pass.; urdf_available=re-verified https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo -- system uses the SMPL-H parametric human body/hand mesh model (via AMASS/MANO), not a robot URDF; no URDF is provided or referenced. Unchanged from prior pass.; urdf_source=same basis as urdf_available -- not_found. Unchanged.; expected_size_gb=https://github.com/brentyi/egoallo download_checkpoint_and_data.sh comment: "egoallo_example_trajectories.zip (8.17 GB)" -- this is the released sample-data package (model checkpoint zip is a separate, smaller 552MB file, not counted here). Field was blank in the prior pass, newly filled.; num_subjects=Not stated anywhere in arXiv:2410.03665 or the GitHub repo for the released example-trajectories package itself (the paper reports subject/scene counts only for third-party evaluation datasets it uses -- AMASS, RICH, Aria Digital Twins, EgoExo4D -- which are separate cataloged datasets, not EgoAllo's own collection). Left blank rather than fabricated.; num_scenes=Same reasoning as num_subjects -- the example-trajectories directory contains multiple named demo sequences (e.g. "coffeemachine") but no enumerated scene count is published. Left blank.; num_objects=No object-level annotation or object count is described in the paper or repo. Left blank.; expected_duration_hours=Total duration of the example-trajectories package is not stated in the repo (only the zip file size, 8.17GB, is given). Left blank rather than estimated.
suggested_new_enum_values: embodiment_class=human_full_body -- EgoAllo estimates whole-body human motion (SMPL-H body pose + height + two-hand pose) from an egocentric head-mounted sensor. None of the existing options fit: 'human_hand' only covers isolated hand embodiment, and the robot-oriented options (single_arm/dual_arm/humanoid/mobile_manipulator) describe robot bodies, not a captured human subject's full body. Re-confirmed on this pass; still no exact match added to EmbodimentClass, so embodiment_class stays blank on the dataset.

name: EgoDex
field_sources: source_url=CORRECTED 2026-07-10 (was arXiv abstract link, moved to paper_url): now points to https://github.com/apple/ml-egodex, the official Apple dataset repo hosting the download links (part1-5/test/extra zips) and Dataset Structure docs, per registry convention that source_url = project/dataset homepage and paper_url = the arXiv paper (see droid.yaml, ego4d.yaml, ego_exo4d.yaml for the same pattern).; paper_url=NEW FIELD, filled: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11709 - "EgoDex: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from Large-Scale Egocentric Video" (Hoque, Huang, Yoon, Sivapurapu, Zhang, 2025). GitHub README explicitly states this repo "accompanies the research paper [EgoDex...]" linking to this arXiv URL.; license=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: GitHub apple/ml-egodex README 'License' section verbatim: "The dataset is available under CC-by-NC-ND terms." arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3.1: "The dataset is publicly available under a CC-by-NC-ND license." Corroborated by third-party HF mirror griffinlabs/EgoDex-LeRobot-v3.0, which tags license:cc-by-nc-nd-4.0. schema.py now defines LicenseEnum.CC_BY_NC_ND_4_0 = "CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0" (the gap previously flagged in suggested_new_enum_values has been closed), so this maps cleanly and the stale suggestion was removed.; raw_format=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: GitHub apple/ml-egodex README 'Dataset Structure': each episode is a paired .hdf5 (skeletal pose transforms, per-joint confidences, camera intrinsics, llm_description language attrs) + .mp4 (video) file with matching numeric index; the structured annotation container is HDF5 (video is a separate peer file, analogous to how LeRobot/ALOHA-style datasets keep video separate from the primary structured container).; release_type=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: fixed_episode_dataset. GitHub README 'Dataset Access and Download': the dataset is a static, versioned set of downloadable zip files (5 training parts + test + extra), not a live generation framework, interactive scene platform, or RL benchmark environment.; collection_method=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3.2 'Data Collection': "All data is collected with Apple Vision Pro running visionOS 2... Production-grade pose tracking software enables natural demonstration with bare hands" -- egocentric human video, no robot involved.; secondary_collection_methods=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, left as []: all 338,000 episodes are collected via the single method described in Sec 3.2 (Apple Vision Pro egocentric capture); no teleop, autonomous-policy, simulation, or synthesis step is described anywhere in arXiv 2505.11709 or the GitHub README.; is_multi_embodiment=NEW FIELD, filled false: the entire dataset is captured via one embodiment class (bare human hands) on one hardware platform (Apple Vision Pro / ARKit). arXiv 2505.11709 abstract and Sec 3.2 describe a single, uniform collection setup with no robot or second embodiment class present.; embodiment_class=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 provides 3D SE(3) pose tracking of human head/upper-body/hand joints via ARKit on Apple Vision Pro; no robot embodiment present anywhere in the dataset.; num_arms=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 4.1: action dimensionality is defined as '2 hands x (3 + 6 + 3x5 fingertips) = 48', i.e. bimanual (both hands) tracked per episode.; gripper_type=NEW FIELD, filled none: no robot gripper is present anywhere in EgoDex; all manipulation is performed with bare human hands (arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3.2, GitHub README). Follows the same convention as sibling bare-hand egocentric datasets (ego_exo4d.yaml, assembly101.yaml, hoi4d.yaml, egoexolearn.yaml all use none).; hand_pose_representation=NEW FIELD, filled keypoints_3d: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3.3 + Appendix A.2 'Complete List of Skeletal Joints': each hand is tracked as 25 named 3D joint transforms (1 wrist + 24 finger sub-joints per hand: IntermediateBase/IntermediateTip/Knuckle/Metacarpal/Tip x4-5 per finger), released as raw SE(3) keypoint transforms in the HDF5 files -- not MANO parameters and not a joint-angle/DoF parameterization. (Being-H0, a third-party downstream project, separately re-fits MANO to these keypoints, but that is not how EgoDex itself represents hand pose.); has_mobile_base=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3 describes the dataset as 'active tabletop manipulation' in a stationary setting, no mobile base.; action_space=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 4.1 'Action Representation': action = 3D position of each wrist + 6D orientation of each wrist + 3D position of each fingertip -- a mix of position and orientation components, not a single joint-angle or single eef-pose vector.; action_frame=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 4.1, verbatim final sentence: "All poses are represented in the camera frame." -- absolute pose per timestep, not a delta relative to the previous frame.; rotation_representation=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 4.1: "the 6D orientation of each wrist (as suggested by [Zhou et al., continuity of rotation representations])" -- 6D rotation used for the wrist-orientation component of the action.; action_dim=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 4.1, verbatim: "each action has a total dimensionality of 2 hands x (3 + 6 + (3 x 5 fingertips)) = 48."; fps=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3.3 modalities: "Egocentric RGB video with 1920x1080 resolution at 30 Hz frequency"; GitHub README: "30 Hz 1080p egocentric video."; fps_variable=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3.3: video, pose, and camera intrinsics/extrinsics are all captured at a fixed 30 Hz; no mention of variable frame rate.; num_camera_views=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3.3 + GitHub README 'Dataset Structure': each episode ships exactly one synthesized head-mounted egocentric RGB .mp4, despite multiple physical cameras being used internally on Vision Pro for SLAM/tracking.; camera_views=Same as num_camera_views -- single head-mounted egocentric viewpoint (Apple Vision Pro). Re-verified 2026-07-10, unchanged.; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=CORRECTED 2026-07-10 (newly set to false; field did not exist in the prior config): GitHub README 'Dataset Structure' shows each episode contains exactly one .hdf5 + one .mp4, with a single camera/intrinsic (3x3, "always the same in every file") -- i.e. only one synthesized camera view is actually released to users. The README's visualize_2d.py note further clarifies "the RGB video is synthesized from multiple cameras on Vision Pro" -- the multiple physical cameras are used internally by ARKit for on-device SLAM/hand-tracking (arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3.2/4.1: "multiple calibrated cameras and on-device SLAM"), but are not exposed as separate synchronized video streams in the released data. Same reasoning as dexcap.yaml (internal multi-camera rig, single released view -> false).; has_camera_calibration=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: GitHub apple/ml-egodex README 'Dataset Structure': HDF5 contains camera/intrinsic (3x3 intrinsics, constant per file) and transforms/camera (per-frame SE(3) extrinsics).; depth_coverage=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: no depth modality is listed in arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3.3 modalities (RGB video, camera intrinsics/extrinsics, 3D joint pose, confidences, language annotation) or in the GitHub README HDF5 structure.; additional_modalities=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, left as []: full-text search of arXiv 2505.11709 for audio/gaze/tactile/force-torque returns zero hits; the 5 modalities listed in Sec 3.3 (RGB video, camera intrinsics/extrinsics, 3D joint pose, pose confidences, language annotation) do not include any of the SensorModality enum values (force_torque, tactile, audio, eye_gaze). Contrast with the sibling ego4d.yaml/ego_exo4d.yaml, which do list audio + eye_gaze because those datasets explicitly capture them.; has_language_instruction=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3.3: "Natural language annotation of the manipulation"; GitHub README: HDF5 attrs f.attrs['llm_description'] / 'llm_description2'.; num_task_types=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 abstract and Sec 3.1: "194 different tabletop tasks" / "contains 829 hours ... with 338000 episodes across 194 tasks."; urdf_available=NEW FIELD, filled false: no robot is present in EgoDex (bare human hand dataset), so no URDF exists for this dataset. Same convention as sibling bare-hand datasets (ego_exo4d.yaml, hoi4d.yaml, assembly101.yaml).; urdf_source=NEW FIELD, filled not_found: consistent with urdf_available=false -- no robot/URDF applicable.; expected_size_gb=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3.1: "The full dataset takes 2.0 TB of storage on disk" (compressed download zips on GitHub README sum to ~1.7 TB across train/test/extra splits).; expected_num_episodes=RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10, unchanged: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3.1: "The EgoDex dataset contains 829 hours of 1080p, 30 Hz egocentric video with 338000 episodes across 194 tasks."; expected_duration_hours=NEW FIELD, filled 829.0: arXiv 2505.11709 abstract and Sec 3.1, verbatim: "EgoDex consists of 829 hours of 30 FPS video..." / "The EgoDex dataset contains 829 hours of 1080p, 30 Hz egocentric video." (GitHub README also gives the train/test/extra split breakdown: ~725h + ~7h + ~97h = 829h.); dof_per_hand=NEW FIELD, checked, left blank: hand pose is released purely as 3D keypoint/joint transforms (25 joints/hand per Appendix A.2), not a joint-angle or DoF parameterization, so there is no stated per-hand DoF figure anywhere in arXiv 2505.11709 or the GitHub README. Same reasoning as ego_exo4d.yaml and assembly101.yaml, which left this blank for an analogous keypoints_3d hand representation.; num_subjects=NEW FIELD, checked, left blank: neither arXiv 2505.11709 nor the GitHub README states a total count of human data collectors/participants (Sec 3.2 'Data Collection' only refers to "the collector"/"data collectors" generically, with no headcount given).; num_scenes=NEW FIELD, checked, left blank: arXiv 2505.11709 Sec 3.5 'Diversity' explicitly states "the scene diversity in EgoDex is limited to tabletop environments" and that the paper's focus is behavioral diversity, not scene diversity -- no numeric count of distinct scenes/locations is given anywhere in the paper or README.; num_objects=NEW FIELD, checked, left blank: no page (arXiv 2505.11709 body, Appendix A.1 task list, Figure 5 'Some of the objects used', GitHub README) states a total distinct-object count for the dataset; Figure 3's object distribution plot is qualitative only (clustering suggested by GPT-4), with no dataset-wide object taxonomy size reported.

name: EgoExoLearn
field_sources: paper_url=CVPR 2024 paper page confirmed via https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16182 (also linked from the GitHub README arxiv badge and the project homepage "Paper" link); source_url=Re-verified 2026-07-10 by curling https://egoexolearn.github.io/ directly (HTTP 200, matches GitHub README project-page badge) - official project homepage, unchanged from prior pass; license=Re-verified 2026-07-10 by fetching https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenGVLab/EgoExoLearn/main/LICENSE directly (HTTP 200, body begins 'MIT License / Copyright (c) 2024 OpenGVLab') and https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/hyf015/EgoExoLearn (cardData.license: "mit"). No separate non-commercial/custom terms found on either the HF card or GitHub repo. Confirmed unchanged: MIT; raw_format=Re-verified 2026-07-10 against https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenGVLab/EgoExoLearn/main/README.md (Data access section - 320p mp4 videos via Google Drive/BaiduYun/HuggingFace, processed gaze .npy files, CLIP/I3D feature files) plus JSON/text annotation files in ./annotations/ - custom directory of MP4 videos + JSON/CSV annotations + .npy gaze arrays, not RLDS/HDF5/LeRobot/ROS_bag/MCAP/TFRecord/VRS. Confirmed unchanged (Custom); release_type=Re-derived 2026-07-10 - EgoExoLearn is a fixed, versioned collection of 747 pre-recorded video sequences (432 ego + 315 exo) with static annotation files distributed via Google Drive/BaiduYun/HuggingFace; it is not a simulation/generation framework, a scene/asset platform, or an RL benchmark environment, so 'fixed_episode_dataset' is correct (arXiv:2403.16182 Section 3.1; GitHub README Data access section); collection_method=Re-verified 2026-07-10 via arXiv:2403.16182 PDF (pdftotext extraction) p.2 'Data collection procedure' - 'one [participant] wears the... Pupil Invisible Glasses, complete[s] the gaze calibration' before recording egocentric task videos; matches 'egocentric_human' directly. Confirmed unchanged; embodiment_class=Re-verified 2026-07-10 via arXiv:2403.16182 abstract/Section 3 (PDF text) - human video dataset (camera wearer's hands/body performing procedural tasks), not a robot; no MANO/skeleton/hand-pose annotations found anywhere in the PDF (grepped 'calibrat', found only gaze calibration, no hand-pose pipeline), so 'human_hand' remains the closest available enum value, consistent with ego4d.yaml/ego_exo4d.yaml precedent. Confirmed unchanged; gripper_type=Re-verified 2026-07-10 - dataset captures bare human hands performing daily/lab tasks with no mechanical end-effector and no hand-pose/MANO annotation pipeline (confirmed absent via full-text search of arXiv:2403.16182 PDF); 'none' applies. Confirmed unchanged; hand_pose_representation=New field, filled 2026-07-10: full-text search of arXiv:2403.16182 PDF found no MANO fits, no 3D keypoint annotations, and no joint-angle data for hands/fingers anywhere in the paper or supplementary (only body-level task/gaze/language annotations exist) - therefore 'none' applies, the same absence-of-data basis used for gripper_type; fps=Re-verified 2026-07-10 via arXiv:2403.16182 PDF (pdftotext) p.2: 'All videos are converted to a constant frame rate of 25fps to ensure uniformity and consistency in our dataset.' Confirmed unchanged; fps_variable=Re-verified 2026-07-10 - same source as fps; the paper explicitly states original capture had variable frame rates (device overheating issues) but all released videos are post-processed/normalized to a single constant 25fps, so fps_variable is false for the released dataset. Confirmed unchanged; camera_views=Re-verified 2026-07-10 via arXiv:2403.16182 PDF (pdftotext) - egocentric videos recorded via head-mounted Pupil Invisible Glasses (head); exocentric demonstration videos are third-person videos, either curated from YouTube for daily tasks or filmed by senior lab members for lab tasks (third_person). Confirmed via full-text search for 'synchron' that the two views are NOT time-synchronized (paper title/abstract: 'Bridging Asynchronous Ego- and Exo-centric View'). Confirmed unchanged; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=New field, filled 2026-07-10: false. The paper's title and abstract explicitly frame the dataset around ASYNCHRONOUS ego/exo pairing - egocentric videos are recorded by participants at a different time/place than the exocentric demonstration video they followed (which for daily tasks is often pre-existing third-party YouTube footage, not filmed by the research team at all). There is no synchronized multi-camera rig (arXiv:2403.16182 title + abstract; Section 3.1); has_camera_calibration=Re-verified 2026-07-10 via arXiv:2403.16182 PDF full-text search for 'calibrat' - the only calibration described is *gaze* calibration for the Pupil Invisible eye-tracker ('complete the gaze calibration', 're-do the gaze calibration'); no camera intrinsics/extrinsics are published, and exocentric demonstration videos are largely third-party YouTube footage with no controlled camera setup. Confirmed unchanged (false); depth_coverage=Re-verified 2026-07-10 - full-text search of arXiv:2403.16182 PDF and GitHub README found no mention of any depth sensor or depth data (only RGB video + gaze + language annotations). Confirmed unchanged (none); additional_modalities=New field, filled 2026-07-10 with [eye_gaze]: arXiv:2403.16182 abstract 'we record high-quality gaze data'; PDF p.2 'one [participant] wears the Pupil Invisible Glasses, complete[s] the gaze calibration... to ensure gaze data fidelity'; GitHub README 'Gaze (processed, npy)' download option and 'we pioneeringly explore the role of gaze in these tasks.' Confirmed unchanged (true); num_task_types=Re-verified 2026-07-10 via arXiv:2403.16182 PDF supplementary S7.4 'Our dataset is collected for 5 types of daily tasks and three types of specialized laboratory tasks' and 'Table S15 shows the names of the 8 tasks' (5 daily + 3 lab = 8). Confirmed unchanged (8); urdf_available=Re-verified 2026-07-10 - no robot hardware of any kind is used or described anywhere in arXiv:2403.16182 or https://github.com/OpenGVLab/EgoExoLearn (purely human video + gaze + language) - therefore no URDF exists. Confirmed unchanged; urdf_source=Same basis as urdf_available - no robot/URDF applicable to this human-video dataset. Confirmed unchanged (not_found); expected_size_gb=CORRECTED 2026-07-10 from 142.0 to 142.7: prior value was eyeballed from the HF 'Files and versions' UI rounding to '142 GB'. Independently queried the HuggingFace Hub API directly (https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/hyf015/EgoExoLearn?expand[]=usedStorage) which returns the exact byte count usedStorage=142677070847 bytes = 142.68 GB (decimal), rounded to 142.7.
