Paper Sec. 3.2 'Repositioning': 'Since objects land in the fixture in a relatively deterministic fashion, we partially script our demonstration collection process while maintaining a certain degree of randomness for the purpose of data diversity.' This applies to the Place_on_fixture and Regrasp primitives (2,250 trajectories each per Table 1, 4,500/22,550 total). Mapping 'partially scripted' collection to the closest enum (autonomous_policy) is an interpretive judgment call; flagged for human review -- arXiv:2401.08553 (Sec. 3.2); is_multi_embodiment=New field, filled (false). Every trajectory across both Single-Object and Multi-Object tasks was collected on the same single Franka Panda arm (Table 1, Sec. 3.5); no other embodiment is described -- arXiv:2401.08553; embodiment_class=Paper Sec. 3.5 and homepage: single Franka Panda arm ('We collected a total of 22,550 trajectories ... on a Franka Panda arm') -- https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/ and arXiv:2401.08553; robot_platform=Homepage: 'We collected a total of 22,550 trajectories across two different tasks on a Franka Panda arm.'; Paper Sec. 3.5: 'We use a Franka Panda robot to collect our dataset' -- https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/ and arXiv:2401.08553; num_arms=Single Franka Panda robot described throughout homepage, dataset page, and paper Sec. 3.5 (Fig. 8: 'a standard Franka arm equipped with four cameras') -- no second arm mentioned anywhere -- https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/; dof_per_arm=Dataset page Data Format: obs/q is a (N, 7) numpy array of joint positions and obs/dq is (N, 7) joint velocities, i.e. 7-DoF Franka Panda arm -- https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/dataset/index.html; gripper_type=Dataset page: obs/gripper_pose is a binary (N,) array (0=open, 1=closed); robot_infra README --gripper_dist flag sets Franka parallel-jaw gripper opening distance -- https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/dataset/index.html and https://github.com/rail-berkeley/fmb/blob/main/robot_infra/README.md; hand_pose_representation=New field, filled (none). Parallel-jaw gripper with only a binary open/closed state (obs/gripper_pose); no dexterous hand, MANO, or keypoint hand-pose data recorded -- consistent with convention used for other parallel-jaw-gripper datasets in this registry -- https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/dataset/index.html; has_mobile_base=Fixed-base Franka Panda arm on a tabletop workspace throughout paper Fig. 8 and homepage videos; no mobile base component described -- arXiv:2401.08553 (Fig. 8) and https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/; action_space=Dataset page: 'action a (N, 7) numpy array of the commanded cartesian action (XYZ, RPY, gripper)'; paper line: '7DoF actions' -- end-effector Cartesian pose/twist command, not joint control -- https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/dataset/index.html and arXiv:2401.08553; action_frame=Re-verified at the code level (stronger evidence than the prior pass): robot_infra/envs/franka_fmb_env.py FrankaFMB.step(action): 'self.nextpos[:3] = self.nextpos[:3] + a' (a = action[:3]) and 'self.nextpos[3:] = (Rotation.from_euler('xyz', action[3:6]) * Rotation.from_quat(self.currpos[3:])).as_quat()' -- the commanded action is explicitly added/composed onto the current pose each control step, confirming delta (not absolute) end-effector control -- https://github.com/rail-berkeley/fmb/blob/main/robot_infra/envs/franka_fmb_env.py and arXiv:2401.08553 (Sec. 3.5, SpaceMouse twist command); rotation_representation=Re-verified at the code level: same franka_fmb_env.py step() composes the rotation delta via Rotation.from_euler('xyz', action[3:6]), i.e. the action's orientation component is an XYZ Euler (RPY) delta rotation, matching the dataset page's 'action a (N, 7) ... (XYZ, RPY, gripper)' description -- https://github.com/rail-berkeley/fmb/blob/main/robot_infra/envs/franka_fmb_env.py and https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/dataset/index.html; action_dim=Dataset page: 'action a (N, 7) numpy array of the commanded cartesian action (XYZ, RPY, gripper)'; paper explicitly states '7DoF actions' -- https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/dataset/index.html and arXiv:2401.08553; fps=Paper Sec. 3.5: SpaceMouse commands are issued at 10 Hz ('command 6 DoF end-effector twist at 10 Hz'); this is the demonstration/action logging rate (separate from the 1 KHz low-level impedance controller) -- arXiv:2401.08553; fps_variable=Paper Sec. 3.5 describes a single fixed 10 Hz teleoperation command rate for all demonstrations, no mention of variable-rate logging -- arXiv:2401.08553; num_camera_views=Paper Sec. 3.5: 'we have four Intel RealSense D405 cameras, two of which are mounted on the robot end-effector, and the rest are placed on each side of the bin'; dataset page lists exactly 4 camera keys (side_1, side_2, wrist_1, wrist_2) -- arXiv:2401.08553 and https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/dataset/index.html; camera_views=Re-verified. Dataset page keys obs/side_1, obs/side_2 (bin-side third-person-style cameras) map to 'side'; obs/wrist_1, obs/wrist_2 (two cameras mounted on the single arm's end-effector, per paper Sec. 3.5 Fig. 7) map to 'wrist'. The CameraView enum in schema.py now includes a first-class WRIST = "wrist" value (added since the prior onboarding pass, which had suggested it as a new enum value under the catch-all "other") -- confirmed still correct, no change needed, and the earlier suggested_new_enum_values entry for this field is now obsolete and removed -- https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/dataset/index.html; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=New field, filled (true). Paper Sec. 3.5: 'In total, we have four Intel RealSense D405 cameras ... We simultaneously capture RGB and depth images from these cameras'; dataset page stores all 4 RGB + 4 depth arrays indexed by the same per-timestep index N within a single trajectory .npy file, confirming frame-synchronized multi-camera capture -- arXiv:2401.08553 (Sec. 3.5) and https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/dataset/index.html; has_camera_calibration=Paper Sec. 3.5: 'we also provide calibrated camera intrinsics. This calibration allows for the conversion of depth images into point clouds'; dataset page provides downloadable intrinsics files for all 4 cameras -- arXiv:2401.08553 and https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/dataset/index.html; depth_coverage=Paper Sec. 3.5: 'We simultaneously capture RGB and depth images from these cameras' (all four); dataset page lists a *_depth array for every one of the 4 camera keys (side_1_depth, side_2_depth, wrist_1_depth, wrist_2_depth) -- full depth coverage across all views -- arXiv:2401.08553 and https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/dataset/index.html; additional_modalities=New field, filled ([force_torque]). Paper Sec. 3.5: 'We also log the end-effector force/torque information provided by the Franka Panda robot'; dataset page keys obs/tcp_force (N,3) and obs/tcp_torque (N,3) confirm this is stored per trajectory (estimated via Franka's internal model, not a dedicated F/T sensor, but still a real logged modality) -- arXiv:2401.08553 (Sec. 3.5) and https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/dataset/index.html; has_language_instruction=CORRECTED from false to true on re-verification. The raw distributed .npy trajectories themselves have no natural-language field (only categorical primitive/object_info labels), which is what the prior pass checked -- but the official FMB GitHub repo also ships fmb_dataset_builder/fmb_dataset/fmb_dataset_dataset_builder.py, which is the sanctioned way to convert this data to RLDS/TFDS for policy training, and it generates a templated natural-language 'language_instruction' (e.g. "Insert the {object} object.", "Regrasp the {object} object.") plus a Universal-Sentence-Encoder 'language_embedding' for every timestep and episode, keyed off primitive + object identity. This is official, code-level evidence of a language-instruction-bearing release path, so the field is corrected to true -- https://github.com/rail-berkeley/fmb/blob/main/fmb_dataset_builder/fmb_dataset/fmb_dataset_dataset_builder.py; num_task_types=Paper explicitly names two top-level tasks: Sec. 3.3 'Single-Object Multi-Stage Manipulation Tasks' and Sec. 3.4 'Multi-Object Multi-Stage Manipulation Tasks'; homepage 'Dataset Overview' likewise presents exactly these two tasks -- arXiv:2401.08553 and https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/; urdf_available=robot_infra README: robot is a standard Franka Emika Panda (or FR3) controlled via libfranka/franka_ros >= 0.8.0, the official Franka Emika ROS stack which ships the manufacturer's franka_description URDF/xacro package for these arms -- https://github.com/rail-berkeley/fmb/blob/main/robot_infra/README.md; urdf_source=Same as above: franka_ros/franka_description is the manufacturer (Franka Emika)-maintained official package, not bundled directly in the FMB repo itself (no .urdf/.xacro files found in rail-berkeley/fmb repo tree) -- https://github.com/rail-berkeley/fmb/blob/main/robot_infra/README.md; expected_size_gb=Dataset page download links: Single-Object Multi-Stage Full Dataset (545GB) + Multi-Object Assembly 1 (86GB) + Assembly 2 (77GB) + Assembly 3 (70GB) = 778GB total -- https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/dataset/index.html; expected_num_episodes=Paper Sec. 3.5 and Table 1: 'the 22,550 demonstration trajectories that we collected and released as part of the benchmark' (Table 1 subtotal column also sums to 22,550); homepage and HF dataset card state the same figure -- arXiv:2401.08553 and https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/; expected_duration_hours=New field, filled (~31.32). Paper Table 1 caption: 'Each trajectory is approximately 5 seconds in length, for a total of 22,550 trajectories.' 22,550 * 5s / 3600 = 31.32 hours; this is an estimate derived from a stated average duration rather than a directly reported total, flagged for human sanity-check -- arXiv:2401.08553 (Table 1 caption, Sec. 3.5); num_objects=New field, filled (66). Homepage/paper Sec. 3.3: Single-Object task uses '54 different assembly objects'; paper Sec. 3.4: Multi-Object task presents 'three sets of more challenging objects for assembly ... each set contains 4 interlocking objects' = 3*4 = 12 objects. Total distinct manipulated objects across both tasks = 54 + 12 = 66 -- arXiv:2401.08553 (Sec. 3.3-3.4) and https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io/

This now follows the same registry-wide convention used by every other embodiment_class=human_hand sibling dataset (assembly101, hot3d, hoi4d, egoexolearn, ego_exo4d, egodex all use gripper_type=none regardless of whether the hand pose is stored as raw keypoints or as a richer MANO parametric fit) - the previous dexterous_hand value was an outlier inconsistent with that convention and has been fixed. Derived from official Meta source code (not directly stated as "DoF" in the paper text, so the derivation is documented explicitly): (1) https://github.com/facebookresearch/hand_tracking_toolkit/blob/main/hand_tracking_toolkit/hand_models/mano_hand_model.py -- MANOHandModel.num_pose_coeffs = 15 (PCA pose components per hand, excluding global wrist orientation/translation which is handled by a separate wrist_xform). (2) https://github.com/facebookresearch/hand_tracking_toolkit/blob/main/hand_tracking_toolkit/hand_models/umetrack_hand_model.py -- NUM_JOINT_FRAMES = 1 (root) + 1 (wrist) + 3*5 (finger frames, 3 per finger x 5 fingers = 15), i.e. 15 finger-articulation frames once the root/wrist frames are excluded. Both hand-pose backends used by HOT3D converge on 15 as the per-hand finger-articulation DoF count (wrist global 6-DoF orientation is tracked separately via wrist_xform in both models, so it is not counted here). Flagged as inferred-from-code rather than paper-stated; moderate confidence.; fps=https://facebookresearch.github.io/hot3d/ (Dataset properties section) -- re-verified: "1.5M multi-view frames (3.7M+ images) recorded at 30 FPS with Project Aria and Quest 3." Unchanged from prior pass.; fps_variable=Same source as fps -- re-verified, 30 FPS is stated as a fixed capture rate for both devices, no mention of variable frame rate. Unchanged from prior pass.; camera_views=https://facebookresearch.github.io/hot3d/ and https://github.com/facebookresearch/hot3d/blob/main/hot3d/clips/README.md -- re-verified: all image streams originate from head-mounted devices (Aria glasses / Quest 3 headset); egocentric head-mounted cameras only, mapped to CameraView.HEAD (no wrist/third-person/top views exist in this dataset). Unchanged from prior pass.; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=Newly filled (true). arXiv:2411.19167 abstract -- "The recordings include multiple synchronized data streams containing egocentric multi-view RGB/monochrome images, eye gaze signal, scene point clouds, and 3D poses of cameras, hands, and objects." Also https://facebookresearch.github.io/hot3d/ section heading "833 minutes of egocentric, multi-view, synchronized recordings," and per-frame *.cameras.json calibration covering multiple simultaneous streams per device (1 RGB + 2 mono for Aria; 2 mono for Quest 3). This is a rigidly-mounted, calibrated, synchronized multi-camera rig (head-worn rather than room-mounted), distinct from the camera_views/HEAD label which only records viewpoint category.; has_camera_calibration=https://github.com/facebookresearch/hot3d/blob/main/hot3d/clips/README.md -- re-verified: each frame ships a <FRAME-ID>.cameras.json with per-stream intrinsic calibration (projection_model_type, projection_params) and extrinsics (T_device_from_camera, T_world_from_camera). Unchanged from prior pass.; depth_coverage=https://facebookresearch.github.io/hot3d/ and arXiv:2411.19167 abstract -- re-verified: no dedicated depth-camera stream is provided for either device; Aria recordings additionally include sparse 3D SLAM scene point clouds (not dense depth maps), which is a distinct modality, so mapped to DepthCoverage.NONE rather than partial/full depth-map coverage. Unchanged from prior pass.; additional_modalities=CORRECTED from [] to [eye_gaze]. The prior pass left this empty; independent re-check of the primary sources shows this was a discrepancy. https://facebookresearch.github.io/hot3d/ (Dataset properties section): "Aria recordings also include 3D scene point clouds from SLAM and eye gaze signal." Confirmed independently by arXiv:2411.19167 abstract: "The recordings include multiple synchronized data streams containing egocentric multi-view RGB/monochrome images, eye gaze signal, scene point clouds, and 3D poses of cameras, hands, and objects." Only Aria (not Quest 3) recordings carry the eye-gaze signal, but since the field is dataset-level and no partial-coverage flag exists, eye_gaze is added as present. SLAM point clouds are not represented by any current SensorModality enum value (force_torque/tactile/audio/eye_gaze) and are not a camera/depth stream, so left unmapped -- see suggested_new_enum_values.; has_language_instruction=https://facebookresearch.github.io/hot3d/, https://github.com/facebookresearch/hot3d, and arXiv:2411.19167 abstract -- re-verified: no natural-language task/instruction annotations are described anywhere on the project page, paper abstract, or toolkit README; only 3D pose/shape ground truth is provided. Unchanged from prior pass.; num_task_types=https://facebookresearch.github.io/hot3d/ (Dataset properties section, "19 subjects, 4 everyday scenarios") -- re-verified: recordings cover simple pick-up/observe/put-down interactions plus kitchen, office, and living-room scenarios (4 scenario categories total). Unchanged from prior pass.; urdf_available=No robot embodiment is present in this dataset, so no URDF applies. Re-verified, unchanged from prior pass.; expected_num_episodes=https://facebookresearch.github.io/hot3d/ (HOT3D-Clips section) -- re-verified with current page text: "There are 3832 clips in total, with 1983 extracted from Aria recordings and 1849 extracted from Quest3 recordings." This is consistent with the prior pass's figure sourced from the clips README (2804 train / 1028 test = 3832 total) -- same grand total of 3832, just cross-tabulated by a different split (Aria/Quest3 device vs train/test). Note: this counts the curated HOT3D-Clips (150-frame / 5s clips); the full VRS-format dataset is instead organized as longer (~2 minute) per-subject recordings whose exact current count was not confirmed from a live, non-stale source.; expected_duration_hours=Newly filled (13.88). arXiv:2411.19167 abstract and https://facebookresearch.github.io/hot3d/ (Dataset properties section) both state "833 minutes ... of recordings." 833 / 60 = 13.883..., rounded to 13.88 hours. This is the full-recordings duration (not just the curated HOT3D-Clips subset).; num_subjects=Newly filled (19). https://facebookresearch.github.io/hot3d/ (Dataset properties section): "19 subjects, 4 everyday scenarios ... we recruited 19 participants with different hand shapes and nationalities." Confirmed independently by arXiv:2411.19167 abstract: "recordings that feature 19 subjects interacting with 33 diverse rigid objects."; num_scenes=Newly filled (4), with a documented caveat. https://facebookresearch.github.io/hot3d/ (Dataset properties section): "In addition to simple pick-up/observe/put-down actions, recordings show scenarios resembling typical actions in a kitchen, office, and living room" (4 scenario types total, same count as num_task_types). Caveat: the same source also states "All scenarios were captured in the same lab with scenario-specific furniture and regularly randomized decorative elements and lighting" -- i.e. physically a single lab space reconfigured 4 ways, not 4 separate physical locations. 4 was chosen as the best-supported reading of "number of distinct recorded scene/scenario configurations," but this could alternatively be read as 1 (single physical lab). Flagged as a genuine ambiguity for human review.; num_objects=Newly filled (33). https://facebookresearch.github.io/hot3d/ (Dataset properties section): "High-fidelity 3D object models -- HOT3D includes high-fidelity 3D models of 33 rigid objects." Confirmed independently by arXiv:2411.19167 abstract: "19 subjects interacting with 33 diverse rigid objects."; release_type=Confirmed via docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-registry-schema-refinement-design.md section 4B, which explicitly classifies hot3d in the "already-confirmed fixed-episode real dataset" bucket mapped to fixed_episode_dataset (a fixed, already-collected set of recordings/clips, not a generation framework, scene platform, or RL benchmark env). Unchanged from prior pass.; raw_format=https://github.com/facebookresearch/hot3d (README) -- re-verified: "An API for downloading and using the full HOT3D dataset provided in a VRS-based format." HOT3D-Clips subset is instead distributed via WebDataset (tar shards) on Hugging Face. VRS is now a first-class RawFormat enum value (added in the 2026-07-10 schema refinement per docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-registry-schema-refinement-design.md section 3.2, citing hot3d as the motivating dataset), so this value is confirmed correct and no longer needs the 'Custom' fallback used in an earlier onboarding pass.
suggested_new_enum_values: license=Dataset license is a custom multi-part CC agreement per https://www.projectaria.com/datasets/hot3d/license/: Sequence data (images/poses from Aria & Quest devices, excluding hand annotations) is CC BY-SA 4.0; Hand annotations are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; 3D object models are CC BY-SA 4.0 with an added no-resale clause. None of the existing LicenseEnum values (CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-NC-4.0, CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, etc.) include the plain ShareAlike (SA, non-NC) clause, and the license is split across data subtypes rather than being a single uniform grant, so this field is left blank rather than forced into an approximate value. This matches the explicit, already-documented limitation in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-registry-schema-refinement-design.md section 3.5, which declined to add a plain CC-BY-SA-4.0 value for this exact reason. Suggest adding CC-BY-SA-4.0 and/or a MIXED/CUSTOM value for datasets with per-component licensing.; hand_pose_representation=HOT3D natively ships two hand-pose formats simultaneously (MANO and UmeTrack/joint_angles), not one. Since this schema field is a single scalar, only one value (mano) could be recorded here. Suggest either converting hand_pose_representation to a List[HandPoseRepresentation] (mirroring additional_modalities/camera_views) or adding a documented convention for "both provided" cases, so the UmeTrack/joint_angles representation is not silently dropped from the record.; additional_modalities=HOT3D's Aria recordings also include dense 3D SLAM scene point clouds (in addition to eye_gaze, which was mapped to the existing enum value). Scene point clouds are neither a depth-camera stream (depth_coverage covers that) nor any current SensorModality value (force_torque, tactile, audio, eye_gaze). Suggest adding a SCENE_POINT_CLOUD / SLAM_POINT_CLOUD SensorModality enum value for datasets like HOT3D that ship SLAM-derived sparse 3D maps alongside images.

name: Humanoid-X
field_sources: paper_url=arXiv:2412.14172 abstract page (Mao et al., 'Learning from Massive Human Videos for Universal Humanoid Pose Control'); license=No explicit license tag on HF dataset card (only 'task_categories: robotics'); dataset README (huggingface.co/datasets/USC-PSI-Lab/Humanoid-X) states original Internet videos are withheld 'to protect copyright' and human-pose subsets are partially withheld 'due to license issues' -> licensing status is unresolved/mixed, mapped to Unknown rather than guessed.; raw_format=HF repo file listing (texts.zip, humanoid_keypoint.zip, humanoid_action.zip, human_pose.zip, train/val/test .txt splits) is a custom zip/txt layout, not RLDS/HDF5/LeRobot/etc.; release_type=Dataset ships a fixed, pre-split set of 176,674 motion-sample IDs (train.txt+val.txt+test.txt line counts verified via direct curl+wc -l on huggingface.co/datasets/USC-PSI-Lab/Humanoid-X resolve URLs), not a generation framework/scene platform/RL-env.; collection_method=Paper abstract (arXiv:2412.14172) describes pipeline: mine Internet human videos -> caption -> retarget human motion to humanoid robot -> RL policy for real-world deployment. This is human video -> robot motion synthesis, not teleop or scripted autonomy. Confirms task hint of human_to_robot_synthesis.; secondary_collection_methods=Paper abstract pipeline step iv ('we employ reinforcement learning to generate physically deployable humanoid actions') and GitHub sihengz02/UH-1 legged_gym/ (Isaac Gym RL training, h1_2_mimic task) show the released humanoid_action.zip data is produced via RL in simulation on top of the retargeted keypoints, hence simulation as a secondary method.; is_multi_embodiment=github.com/sihengz02/UH-1 legged_gym/legged_gym/envs/ contains only a base/ and h1_2/ robot config (no other robot folders); the released RL-generated actions and mimic policy target only Unitree H1_2. (Note: a separate helper repo, song-siqi/retarget2humanoid, mentions generic retargeting support for Unitree G1, but that is not part of the Humanoid-X released data/pipeline itself.); embodiment_class=Per task instructions and paper: source data is human video/pose, retargeted onto a bipedal humanoid robot (Unitree H1_2); released keypoint/action data represents robot embodiment, so humanoid (not human_hand).; robot_platform=github.com/sihengz02/UH-1 legged_gym/legged_gym/envs/h1_2/ (h1_2_mimic.py, h1_2_legged_robot_config.py) and README's 'python play.py ... --task h1_2_mimic' show target robot is Unitree H1_2. Enum has no h1_2-specific value; mapped to closest existing value unitree_h1 (see suggested_new_enum_values).; num_arms=Confirmed by official Unitree H1_2 URDF (github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_gym resources/robots/h1_2/h1_2.urdf): left_*/right_* shoulder/elbow/wrist joint sets -> 2 arms.; dof_per_arm=Official Unitree H1_2 URDF (unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_gym, h1_2.urdf) lists 7 revolute joints per arm (shoulder pitch/roll/yaw, elbow pitch/roll, wrist pitch/yaw = 7); combined with 12 leg + 1 torso DOF this sums to 27, matching num_actions=27 in UH-1's h1_2_mimic_config.py exactly (body-only, no hand joints).; gripper_type=UH-1's h1_2_mimic_config.py sets num_actions/num_policy_actions=27, matching the 27 body-only DOF (12 leg + 1 torso + 14 arm) of the official H1_2 URDF with no finger/hand joints included -> no gripper/hand actuation in the released action space.; hand_pose_representation=Same as gripper_type: released keypoint (34-dim = 27 DoF joint pose + 3 root pos + 4 root quat, per github.com/sihengz02/UH-1 README inference section) and action (27-dim) data contain no finger/hand pose channels.; has_mobile_base=Unitree H1_2 is a bipedal legged humanoid (legs+torso+arms per official URDF), not a wheeled/tracked mobile base.; action_space=github.com/sihengz02/UH-1 legged_gym/legged_gym/envs/h1_2/h1_2_legged_robot_config.py: 'class control: control_type = "P" # P: position, V: velocity, T: torques' -> policy outputs joint position targets for a PD controller.; action_frame=h1_2_legged_robot.py _compute_torques(): 'torques = p_gains*(actions_scaled + default_dof_pos_all - dof_pos) - ...' i.e. action is a delta added to the default/nominal joint pose, not an absolute target.; rotation_representation=github.com/sihengz02/UH-1 top-level README inference section: generated keypoint is '[num_frames, 34-dim]' where '34-dim = 27-dim DoFs + 3-dim root position + 4-dim root orientation'; a 4-dim orientation is a quaternion.; action_dim=UH-1 h1_2_mimic_config.py: num_actions = num_policy_actions = 27 (body-only DOF, matches official H1_2 URDF joint count of 12 leg + 1 torso + 14 arm).; num_camera_views/camera_views/has_synchronized_multiview_rig/has_camera_calibration=HF README explicitly states original Internet source videos are NOT released ('We will not release the original Internet videos to protect copyright'); source videos were ordinary single monocular Internet clips (per arXiv abstract 'data mining from the Internet'), not a synchronized/calibrated multi-camera rig, and no camera imagery ships in the released dataset at all.; depth_coverage=3D human pose is estimated from monocular RGB Internet video (paper pipeline step ii / README-Humanoid-X.md '3D Human Pose Estimation' referencing VIBE/4D-Humans, both monocular-RGB methods); no depth sensor data involved.; has_language_instruction=HF dataset card + README: 'we fully release the text description data texts.zip'; paper: dataset is pairs of <video, Text, human pose, robot pose, robot action> with text-based motion descriptions used to train UH-1 (text -> action).; urdf_available/urdf_source=Unitree officially publishes the H1_2 URDF at github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_gym (resources/robots/h1_2/h1_2.urdf), an official Unitree Robotics GitHub org repo.; expected_size_gb=HF Hub API (api/datasets/USC-PSI-Lab/Humanoid-X) field 'usedStorage': 41262884599 bytes ~= 41.26 GB (decimal).; expected_num_episodes=Direct line count of train.txt (141341) + val.txt (8827) + test.txt (26506) = all.txt (176674), fetched via curl+wc -l from huggingface.co/datasets/USC-PSI-Lab/Humanoid-X resolve/main/. Note: the project homepage (usc-gvl.github.io/UH-1, now redirecting to physical-superintelligence-lab.github.io/UH-1) states the dataset 'consists of 163,800 pairs of motion samples', which does not match the directly counted file totals; the counted value (176,674) was preferred as it is independently verifiable from the actual released split files rather than a possibly-stale project-page figure.
suggested_new_enum_values: robot_platform=unitree_h1_2 — Humanoid-X/UH-1 specifically targets the Unitree H1_2 variant (27 body DOF: 12 leg + 1 torso + 14 arm per official unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_gym h1_2.urdf), which is materially different from the base Unitree H1 (19 DOF per unitreerobotics/unitree_ros h1_description). The current enum only offers the generic 'unitree_h1', losing this distinction; recommend adding a separate 'unitree_h1_2' value.

suggested_new_enum_values: GripperType=Add MIXED = "mixed": this dataset combines parallel_jaw (Panda-gripper subsets), dexterous_hand (PandaDexRH/GR1/Unitree-G1 subsets), and gripper-less arms-only manipulation within a single dataset release, and the schema's gripper_type field is a single Optional[GripperType] with no way to represent a genuinely mixed release short of leaving it blank (which loses information relative to what's knowable per-subset).; RotationRepresentation=Add MIXED = "mixed": this dataset combines subsets with none (pure joint-position GR1/gr1_arms_waist subsets, no wrist orientation encoding at all) and subsets with quaternion (unitree_g1's observation.eef_state/action.eef "_abs_quat" fields) within a single release. name: OVMM
field_sources: paper_url=arXiv abstract page https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.11565 (HomeRobot: Open-Vocabulary Mobile Manipulation); license=HSSD scene dataset (used for all OVMM sim scenes) is licensed CC-BY-NC-4.0 per https://huggingface.co/datasets/hssd/hssd-hab README/cardData; note the HomeRobot *code* repo (facebookresearch/home-robot) is separately MIT-licensed per its LICENSE file, but the dataset assets inherit HSSD's CC-BY-NC-4.0.; raw_format=HF dataset ai-habitat/OVMM_episodes stores episodes as train/val/minival *.json.gz plus transformations.npy/viewpoints.npy; ai-habitat/OVMM_objects stores .glb meshes, csv metadata, and a pickle of CLIP embeddings -- none of the schema's named formats (RLDS/HDF5/LeRobot/ROS_bag/MCAP/TFRecord/VRS) match, so classified as Custom.; release_type=arXiv paper: benchmark provides RL + heuristic baselines trained/evaluated via an EvalAI challenge (CVPR 2024 HomeRobot OVMM Challenge), i.e. an RL benchmark environment rather than a fixed static episode dump.; collection_method=arXiv paper Sec 3.1/App D: sim episodes are procedurally generated in the AI Habitat simulator over HSSD scenes (episode generation places objects/receptacles programmatically, not via teleoperated demonstrations).; secondary_collection_methods=arXiv paper: object/receptacle set is aggregated and manually curated/annotated from AI2-THOR, Amazon-Berkeley Objects, Google Scanned Objects and HSSD (scene_asset_curation); real-world and sim baselines are evaluated by running heuristic/RL autonomous policies in the loop rather than human teleop (autonomous_policy).; is_multi_embodiment=Only one physical embodiment (Hello Robot Stretch with DexWrist) is used for both the real-world stack and as the basis for the simulated agent's action/observation space in the paper; home-robot repo's minimal Spot support is a separate example package, not part of the OVMM benchmark itself.; embodiment_class=arXiv paper: Hello Robot Stretch is a wheeled mobile base with a single telescoping arm -- fits mobile_manipulator.; robot_platform=arXiv paper Sec 3.2 ('We use the Hello Robot Stretch [22] with DexWrist...'); Hello Robot Stretch is not present in the RobotPlatform enum, so set to other (see suggested_new_enum_values).; num_arms=arXiv paper: Stretch has a single telescoping arm.; dof_per_arm=arXiv paper Sec 3.2, direct quote: Stretch with DexWrist '...offers 6 DoF manipulation'.; gripper_type=arXiv paper App D/E: heuristic grasping policy 'assumes a parallel gripper performing top-down grasps'.; hand_pose_representation=No dexterous hand; Stretch uses a simple parallel-jaw gripper, so hand_pose_representation is not applicable.; has_mobile_base=arXiv paper: Stretch is a wheeled mobile manipulator; actions include base translation/rotation waypoints.; action_space=arXiv paper App D.6/E.3: actions are 'base translation and rotation waypoints, all arm joints (arm extension, arm lift, gripper yaw, pitch, and roll)' -- a mix of base pose and arm joint-position commands, so classified as mixed.; action_frame=arXiv paper App F: per-step action magnitudes are explicitly bounded increments (e.g. 'arm's extension and lift can be changed by at most 2-10cm in a single step', head/gripper joints by 0.02-0.1 rad, base by 10-25cm or 5-30 degrees), i.e. delta/incremental actions.; rotation_representation=arXiv paper: wrist/gripper orientation is commanded via separate yaw/pitch/roll joint values, i.e. an Euler-angle-style decomposition.; num_camera_views=arXiv paper App F.2/F.3: observations consistently reference a single 'robot head camera' (RGB-D + semantic segmentation); no wrist or other camera is described.; camera_views=Same as num_camera_views -- only the head-mounted RGB-D camera is described in the paper.; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=Only a single camera view is used, so there is no multiview rig.; depth_coverage=arXiv paper: depth from the head camera is used throughout for perception/mapping (e.g. 'Robot head camera depth...').; has_language_instruction=arXiv paper Sec 6 (Discussion/Limitations), direct quote: 'We also currently consider full natural language queries out-of-scope.' Task goals are specified via structured object_category/start_recep_category/goal_recep_category fields (see HF README for ai-habitat/OVMM_episodes), not free-form language instructions.; num_task_types=arXiv paper: single task template of the form 'move the <object> from the <start_receptacle> to the <goal_receptacle>' (Open-Vocabulary Mobile Manipulation / pick-and-place rearrangement).; urdf_available=home-robot GitHub repo ships assets/hab_stretch/urdf/hab_stretch.urdf (verified reachable at raw.githubusercontent.com/facebookresearch/home-robot/main/assets/hab_stretch/urdf/hab_stretch.urdf).; urdf_source=URDF is bundled directly in the facebookresearch/home-robot repo (assets/hab_stretch/urdf/), which backs this dataset/benchmark.; num_scenes=arXiv paper App D.1, direct quote: 'these are divided into train, validation, and test splits of 38, 12, and 10 scenes each' = 60 total HSSD scenes used for the OVMM sim benchmark; corroborated by ai-habitat/OVMM_episodes HF repo file listing (38 train/content/*.json.gz scene files plus combined val/minival episode files).; num_objects=arXiv paper App D.1, direct quote: 'In total, we annotated 2,535 objects from 129 total categories' (plus 21 separate receptacle categories, consistent with Table 1's '150 Cats' = 129 object + 21 receptacle categories).
suggested_new_enum_values: robot_platform=hello_robot_stretch -- Hello Robot Stretch (with DexWrist) is the real-world mobile-manipulator platform used by OVMM/HomeRobot and by several other Stretch-based datasets; not currently in the RobotPlatform enum, so this config falls back to 'other'.

name: PH2D
field_sources: source_url=Pre-filled stub, verified reachable via HF datasets API https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/RogerQi/PH2D (sha=87b77716f10c04602bdf53de4657795b13fde1c5, not gated, not private).; paper_url=arXiv:2503.13441, "Humanoid Policy ~ Human Policy" (Qiu, Yang, Cheng, Chawla, Li, He, Yan, Yoon, Hoque, Paulsen, Yang, Zhang, Yi, Shi, Wang). HF dataset card verbatim: "arXiv link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.13441". CoRL paper PDF also linked from https://human-as-robot.github.io/.; license=HF dataset card front-matter: "license: mit"; HF API cardData.license == "mit"; schema.org JSON-LD on the dataset page: "license": "https://choosealicense.com/licenses/mit/".; raw_format=HF README "Data organizations": "Each folder represents one task. III-A "Data Collection Pipeline": "We collect task-oriented egocentric human demonstrations by asking human operators to perform tasks... when wearing the VR devices" (Apple Vision Pro built-in camera + ARKit, or Meta Quest 3 / Apple Vision Pro + ZED Mini stereo camera). Per paper Table I, the human-collected portion is the dominant share of the dataset (26,824 of 28,376 demos, ~94.5% of episodes; ~3.02M of ~3.69M frames, ~82% of frames), so egocentric_human is used as the primary collection_method.; secondary_collection_methods=GitHub RogerQi/human-policy README "Download open-sourced data": the HF release also contains "Two Unitree H1 humanoid robots physically located in UCSD and CMU. Collected via teleoperation" (real-robot portion, task IDs not starting with "1" per HF README convention) and "One Unitree H1 humanoid robot in Mujoco. Collected via teleoperation" (sim portion). teleop covers both the real-robot and Mujoco-teleoperated episodes; simulation is added separately because ph2d_metadata.json embodiment_type_camera lists explicit sim-only embodiment types (h1_inspire_sim, h1_2_inspire_sim, gr1_inspire_sim) and the HF file listing includes sim-only folders (000-sim_test/, 1061new_sim_pepsi_grasp_h1_2_inspire-.../).; is_multi_embodiment=true: the released dataset genuinely mixes two physically distinct capture setups -- real human bodies wearing consumer VR/AR headsets (embodiment_type human_avp / human_zed in ph2d_metadata.json) and real/simulated Unitree H1 (and one Fourier-GR1-class sim variant, gr1_inspire_sim) humanoid robots (embodiment_type h1_inspire / h1_2_inspire_cmu / h1_inspire_sim / h1_2_inspire_sim) -- unlike single-embodiment human-to-robot-synthesis datasets in this registry (e.g. dexcap.yaml) that only ever release one target robot's data.; embodiment_class=JUDGMENT CALL, human_hand: PH2D is genuinely bi-embodiment (human + Unitree H1 humanoid, see is_multi_embodiment above), and the EmbodimentClass enum only allows one scalar value here. Chosen human_hand because it is the dominant raw-capture format by volume (arXiv:2503.13441 Table I: 26,824/28,376 demos and ~3.02M/~3.69M frames are the human-collected portion), matching the same "dominant collected format" convention already used for dexcap.yaml (also embodiment_class=human_hand despite robot_platform=franka_panda being filled for the robot side). robot_platform=unitree_h1, gripper_type=dexterous_hand, dof_per_arm/dof_per_hand below describe the humanoid-robot side of this same dataset; a reviewer could reasonably prefer embodiment_class=humanoid instead since the paper's stated goal and dataset name ("Physical Humanoid-Human Data") center on humanoid robot policy learning -- flagging this ambiguity explicitly for human review.; robot_platform=arXiv:2503.13441 "Hardware Platforms" paragraph: "We run our experiments on Unitree H1 bimanual humanoid robots equipped with a pair of 6-DOF Inspire dexterous hands." GitHub README also states two real Unitree H1 robots (UCSD + CMU) plus one Mujoco-simulated Unitree H1 were used for the released robot-side data. (ph2d_metadata.json also lists a minor gr1_inspire_sim embodiment_type for one sim task folder -- Fourier GR1-class -- but Unitree H1 is the paper's stated primary/majority hardware platform.); num_arms=arXiv:2503.13441 "Hardware Platforms": bimanual Unitree H1 ("a pair of 6-DOF Inspire dexterous hands"); "Unified State-Action Space" section: "Both bimanual robots and humans have two end effectors." -> 2 arms for both embodiments.; dof_per_arm=arXiv:2503.13441 "Hardware Platforms": "This configuration results in a total of 28 degrees of freedom" = 2 arms x 7 DoF + 2 hands x 6 DoF + 2 DoF neck = 14+12+2=28, confirming 7 DoF per arm. Cross-checked against GitHub RogerQi/human-policy hdt/constants.py H1_QPOS_LEFT_ARM_INDICES = elbow(4 indices)+wrist(3 indices) = 7.; dof_per_hand=arXiv:2503.13441 "Hardware Platforms", verbatim: "a pair of 6-DOF Inspire dexterous hands." Cross-checked against hdt/constants.py H1_QPOS_LEFT_HAND_INDICES / H1_QPOS_RIGHT_HAND_INDICES, each 6 indices long (the real-robot control interface after truncating to the 26-dim actuated H1_MOTOR_INDICES).; gripper_type=Same source as dof_per_hand: Unitree H1 robots are equipped with 6-DOF Inspire dexterous hands (arXiv:2503.13441 "Hardware Platforms"), not parallel-jaw grippers.; hand_pose_representation=arXiv:2503.13441 "Unified State-Action Space": "The HAT model makes predictions in a human-centric action space using wrist 6 DoF poses and finger tips" (finger tips = 3D keypoints, not joint angles or MANO parameters). Confirmed in GitHub hdt/constants.py: RETARGETTING_INDICES / VALID_RETARGETTING_INDICES select 5 fingertip keypoints per hand, and OUTPUT_LEFT_KEYPOINTS/OUTPUT_RIGHT_KEYPOINTS each span 3*5=15 dims (3D xyz per fingertip keypoint) within the 128-dim ACTION_STATE_VEC_SIZE.; has_mobile_base=arXiv:2503.13441 "Hardware Platforms": "We focus on manipulation and do not actuate the lower body of the robot." No locomotion/mobile base is used in this dataset -- the H1's legs are fixed/unused, only upper body + a 2-DoF actuated neck are actuated.; action_space=arXiv:2503.13441 "Unified State-Action Space" + hdt/constants.py ACTION_STATE_VEC_SIZE=128 breakdown: "9 (position_3+rotation_6) + 3*6 + 9 + 3*6 + 9" per side -- i.e. the unified action combines 6-DoF end-effector/head poses (position+rotation) with 3D fingertip keypoints and (for the robot) 26-dim actuated qpos, a mix of eef_pose and joint/keypoint components -> mixed.; action_frame=JUDGMENT CALL, absolute: arXiv:2503.13441 "Adapting Low-cost Commercial Devices" section states devices provide "accurate on-device world frame 3D head pose tracking and 3D hand keypoint tracking" -- poses are tracked in a consistent world frame per timestep rather than as inter-frame deltas. The paper does not explicitly use the words "absolute" or "delta" for the released action representation, so this is inferred by analogy to the same "world/camera frame per-timestep pose" pattern used for the absolute classification in egodex.yaml and dexcap.yaml.; rotation_representation=GitHub hdt/constants.py, verbatim comment: "HDT training state space indices (128-dim) ... 9(position_3 +rotation_6) + 3*6 + 9 + 3*6 + 9" -- each 9-dim eef/head block is 3D position + 6D rotation, i.e. the 6D continuous rotation representation (Zhou et al.), matching the "6 DoF poses" language in arXiv:2503.13441 "Unified State-Action Space".; state_dim=GitHub hdt/constants.py: "ACTION_STATE_VEC_SIZE = 128" -- the unified HDT/HAT training state-action vector size described in arXiv:2503.13441 "Unified State-Action Space" section, applied to both human and humanoid-robot embodiments.; action_dim=Same source as state_dim: hdt/constants.py ACTION_STATE_VEC_SIZE = 128 is used for both the state and action representation in the unified human-humanoid space (OUTPUT_INDEX in the same file selects the action-relevant subset of this 128-dim vector).; fps=arXiv:2503.13441 Table I footnote, verbatim: "The number of frames is estimated assuming 30 Hz."; fps_variable=Inferred false: Table I footnote treats 30 Hz as a fixed assumed capture rate for computing frame counts across the whole released dataset (both human and robot portions); no mention of variable frame rate anywhere in the paper or GitHub README.; num_camera_views=arXiv:2503.13441 "Adapting Low-cost Commercial Devices": each data-collection device (Apple Vision Pro built-in camera, or Meta Quest 3/Vision Pro + ZED Mini stereo camera holder) provides a single head-mounted egocentric camera stream per episode; depth_coverage=Inferred none: arXiv:2503.13441 "Unified State-Action Space" states "The images are encoded by a frozen DinoV2 encoder" (an RGB image encoder); no depth map or point-cloud modality is mentioned anywhere in the paper despite the ZED stereo camera hardware being capable of depth -- only RGB frames appear to be used/released.; additional_modalities=Checked: full-text search of arXiv:2503.13441 for force/torque, tactile, audio, and eye-gaze sensing returns no hits describing these as recorded/released modalities (Apple ARKit head/hand tracking and RGB video are the only sensing channels described).; has_language_instruction=HF README "Data organizations": "Most HDF5 files contain ONE execution of the task specified by the language..." -- each episode is associated with a language task description.; num_task_types=ph2d_metadata.json "metadata.task_types" list, verbatim: ["pouring", "grasping", "stacking", "picking", "cup_passing", "sorting_cans"] = 6 task types.; urdf_available=GitHub RogerQi/human-policy README "Repo Structure": "assets: robot URDFs and meshes" -- the companion code repo linked from the HF dataset card (and from https://human-as-robot.github.io/) bundles Unitree H1 (and Inspire hand) URDFs used for Mujoco simulation/replay (docs/humanoid_mujoco.md).; urdf_source=Same GitHub repository (RogerQi/human-policy) linked from the HF dataset card as the official code/data companion repo, consistent with the dataset_repo convention used for arcap.yaml/dexcap.yaml.; expected_size_gb=HF datasets API https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/RogerQi/PH2D field "usedStorage": 15829946918 bytes = 15.83 GB (decimal GB convention, same convention used for dexcap.yaml/arcap.yaml).; expected_num_episodes=arXiv:2503.13441 Table I ("Comparison to prior work"), PH2D row: Human 26,824 demos + Robot 1,552 demos = 28,376 total demos/episodes (exact counts as stated in the table; only the frame counts in the same row are marked approximate with "~").; expected_duration_hours=DERIVED, approximate: arXiv:2503.13441 Table I gives ~3.02M human frames + ~668k robot frames = ~3.69M total frames, and the same table's footnote states frame counts are "estimated assuming 30 Hz." 3.69M frames / 30 fps / 3600 s/hr ~= 34.1 hours. No total-duration figure is stated directly in the paper; this is a basic arithmetic derivation from the paper's own approximate frame counts and stated fps, not an independently fabricated number.; num_subjects=Checked, left blank: neither arXiv:2503.13441 nor the GitHub README states a total headcount of human data collectors/operators (Sec. III-A refers generically to "human operators"; HF task folder names like "104-lars-grasping..." suggest multiple named operators but give no aggregate count).; num_scenes=Checked, left blank: arXiv:2503.13441 "Human data improves background generalization" section only states qualitatively that "the human data includes more than five different backgrounds" for one ablation task (cup passing); no dataset-wide scene/background count is given.; num_objects=Checked, left blank: the paper repeatedly refers to "a diverse set of objects" (Table I caption) and names specific objects used in ablations (bottle, box_1, box_2, can, coke, etc.) but never states a total distinct-object count across the released dataset.

name: PokeFlex
field_sources: license=ETH Zurich institutional Terms of Use at https://pokeflex.ait.ethz.ch/ (registration-gated download page): custom EULA, non-exclusive/non-transferable/non-sub-licensable, non-commercial academic use only, redistribution and re-packaging prohibited, revocable by ETH on request, no standard CC license text used -> mapped to Proprietary (see suggested_new_enum_values for a more precise category).; raw_format=GitHub repo https://github.com/pokeflex-dataset/reconstruction, dataset/preprocess.py: data is organized as per-take folders with per-camera subfolders (volucam/, kinect/, realsense/), color/depth images, camera_parameters.json (intrinsics/extrinsics), and robot_data records with frame/forces fields -- no standard RLDS/HDF5/LeRobot/ROS_bag/MCAP/TFRecord/VRS container is used.; release_type=Project page + arXiv:2410.07688 abstract: fixed set of 18 objects with a fixed number of recorded poking/dropping sequences, released as a static downloadable dataset (not a generation framework, scene platform, or RL benchmark env).; is_multi_embodiment=arXiv:2410.07688 Sec 3.1 / project page: single robotic manipulator used throughout the poking protocol; dropping protocol uses no robot (free-fall onto a flat surface).; embodiment_class=arXiv:2410.07688 Sec 3.1 and Fig. 3/4: 'a robotic manipulator that pokes objects with a transparent acrylic stick' -- single arm, brand/model not disclosed in paper, website, or GitHub repo.; num_arms=Same as embodiment_class source -- one manipulator is used.; gripper_type=arXiv:2410.07688 Sec 3.1: the end-effector is a rigid transparent acrylic poking stick, not a gripper -- mapped to GripperType.NONE.; hand_pose_representation=No dexterous hand or bare-hand tracking is present anywhere in the dataset (rigid stick end-effector only) -- mapped to HandPoseRepresentation.NONE.; has_mobile_base=Paper describes the manipulator as fixed inside the multi-view volumetric capture system (MVS) studio rig; no mobile base is mentioned.; action_space=arXiv:2410.07688 Sec 3.1 (ar5iv full text): 'The robot logs end-effector poses, interaction forces and torques at 120 Hz.' Applies only to the poking-protocol sequences (not the dropping protocol, which has no robot); this is closer to logged robot state during a scripted probing motion than a policy-commanded action, flagged here for human review.; fps=arXiv:2410.07688 Sec 3.1: 'We record data at 30 fps and 60 fps for the poking and dropping protocols, respectively.' 30 fps (poking, the richer/primary protocol) used as representative value; fps_variable set true because dropping uses 60 fps.; fps_variable=Same source as fps -- two different frame rates are used depending on protocol (poking vs dropping).; num_camera_views=arXiv:2410.07688 Table 1 and Sec 3.1: poking sequences record 2 Volucam RGB cameras (from the MVS) + 2 Intel RealSense D405 RGB-D (eye-in-hand, robot end-effector mounted) + 2 Azure Kinect RGB-D (eye-to-hand, opposing external viewpoints) = 6 released per-frame camera streams. Dropping sequences use only the 2 Volucam cameras (no depth, no robot cams) -- 6 reflects the richer poking-protocol setup; see camera_views mapping caveat below.; camera_views=Mapped from arXiv:2410.07688 Sec 3.1: RealSense D405 (eye-in-hand, mounted on robot end-effector) -> wrist; Azure Kinect (eye-to-hand, opposing external viewpoints) -> third_person; Volucam cameras (2 of the 106-camera 360 deg volumetric capture rig, from Collet et al. 2015-style MVS) -> other, since they do not fit any single fixed viewpoint category cleanly.; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=arXiv:2410.07688 Sec 3.1: all cameras/robot are hardware-synchronized via a shared Linear Timecode (LTC) signal from an Atomos Ultrasync device, with a leader/follower camera architecture.; has_camera_calibration=arXiv:2410.07688 Table 1: 'Camera intrinsic and extrinsic parameters check'; confirmed in repo dataset/preprocess.py, which loads camera_parameters.json per camera with intrinsics/extrinsics.; depth_coverage=Depth is only available from the RealSense D405 and Azure Kinect cameras during the poking protocol; the Volucam RGB cameras (used in both protocols, and the only cameras in the dropping protocol) have no per-pixel depth channel -- coverage across the full dataset is partial, not full.; additional_modalities=arXiv:2410.07688 Table 1 / Sec 3.1: 'Estimated 3D contact forces and torques' logged at 120 Hz during poking -- mapped to SensorModality.FORCE_TORQUE. No tactile, audio, or eye-gaze modalities are mentioned anywhere.; has_language_instruction=No language annotation, instruction, or task description field is mentioned anywhere on the project page, arXiv paper (checked via full-text search), or GitHub repo.; num_task_types=Two distinct data-collection protocols are described: poking (robot-induced deformation) and dropping (free-fall deformation) -- arXiv:2410.07688 Sec 3.1. Not manipulation 'skill' task types in the usual VLA sense; flagged for human review.; urdf_available=No URDF, robot model, or CAD file is present in the GitHub repo (https://github.com/pokeflex-dataset/reconstruction directory listing: assets/, config/, dataset/, models/, test/, training/, README.md) nor referenced on the project page or in the paper. Robot brand/model itself is never disclosed.; num_scenes=All data is captured inside a single fixed professional multi-view volumetric capture system (MVS) studio setup -- arXiv:2410.07688 Sec 3.1.; num_objects=Project page and arXiv:2410.07688 abstract: 'PokeFlex consists of 18 deformable objects' (13 everyday items + 5 3D-printed objects).
suggested_new_enum_values: license=custom_gated_research_only -- a registration-gated, revocable, non-transferable institutional EULA (ETH Zurich) that prohibits ANY redistribution (even non-commercial) and is not literally a Creative Commons license, distinct from generic 'Proprietary'.; collection_method=scripted_robot_probing -- a non-learned, pre-programmed/randomized robot-arm motion (e.g., poking objects with a rigid tool along randomized trajectories) used purely for automated real-world data collection; distinct from teleop (no human control), autonomous_policy (not a learned closed-loop policy), and simulation. PokeFlex's poking protocol needs this category; left collection_method blank because none of the existing CollectionMethod values fit.

name: RoboCasa
field_sources: license=GitHub robocasa/robocasa README.md 'License' section (reconfirmed verbatim): 'Code: MIT License ... Assets and Datasets: CC BY 4.0'; docs using_datasets.html has an identical License section. Dataset assets are CC-BY-4.0.; raw_format=robocasa.ai/docs using_datasets.html 'Dataset structure': datasets are distributed as LeRobot-format dirs (meta/, data/*.parquet, videos/*.mp4), produced by robocasa/scripts/dataset_scripts/convert_hdf5_lerobot.py from internal HDF5; confirmed by reading that script directly on GitHub (creates a LerobotDatasetWrapper dataset).; release_type=Confirmed fixed_episode_dataset. RoboCasa/robosuite is a simulation+generation framework (MimicGen can synthesize more demos), but download_datasets.py + dataset_registry.py distribute a concrete, versioned (v1.0) set of pre-generated per-task HDF5/LeRobot demo files hosted on Box; this registry entry tracks that fixed released artifact (655k episodes), matching the precedent in configs/dexmimicgen.yaml and configs/libero.yaml for framework-backed fixed releases.; collection_method=arXiv:2603.04356 (RoboCasa365) Sec 3.4.1-3.4.3, re-verified in full text: 30k (pretrain) + 25k (target) = 55k human-teleoperated seed demos, then MimicGen generates 60 atomic tasks x 10k demos = 600k synthetic demos from those seeds -- ~92% of the 655k total is MimicGen-synthesized from human seeds, matching 'human_to_robot_synthesis' (same convention as configs/mimicgen.yaml, configs/dexmimicgen.yaml).; secondary_collection_methods=CORRECTED from [] to [teleop]. Same source as collection_method: the 55k human seed demos (8.4% of the 655k released total) are genuine teleoperation data that is itself separately downloadable (download_datasets.py --source human), not just an internal-only seed step -- matching the configs/mimicgen.yaml precedent (there, an even smaller 0.2% teleop-seed fraction was still recorded as a secondary method), more clearly warranted here given the larger fraction.; is_multi_embodiment=Newly filled: false. arXiv:2603.04356 Sec 3.4.1: 'For our data collection, we use the Franka Panda Emika robot, equipped with an Omron mobile base ... in principle, our simulation framework CAN SUPPORT data collection with other mobile manipulators and humanoid platforms' -- the actual released dataset uses only one embodiment (PandaOmron); the multi-embodiment capability is a framework property, not something realized in the released data.; embodiment_class=arXiv:2603.04356 Sec 3.4.1: single Franka Panda arm on an actuated Omron wheeled mobile base (re-confirmed unchanged).; robot_platform=Same source; Franka Panda is the closest enum match for the arm component. The Omron mobile base has no dedicated enum value and is captured via has_mobile_base (re-confirmed unchanged).; num_arms=Confirmed via robocasa/models/assets/groot_dataset_assets/PandaOmron_modality.json and dataset_registry.py: single-arm 'PandaOmron' robot model throughout (re-confirmed).; dof_per_arm=Franka Emika Panda manufacturer spec: 7 revolute joints, unmodified by RoboCasa's PandaOmron model (re-confirmed unchanged).; gripper_type=robocasa/environments/kitchen/kitchen.py default gripper_types='default' resolves to robosuite's stock 2-finger PandaGripper (re-confirmed unchanged).; has_mobile_base=arXiv:2603.04356 Sec 3.4.1 + robot_type='PandaOmron' in convert_hdf5_lerobot.py; action.base_motion and state.base_position/base_rotation fields in PandaOmron_modality.json directly confirm an actuated mobile base (re-confirmed unchanged).; action_space=robocasa/models/assets/groot_dataset_assets/PandaOmron_modality.json (fetched directly from GitHub main): action vector = base_motion(4) + control_mode(1) + end_effector_position(3) + end_effector_rotation(3) + gripper_close(1) = 12 dims -- eef pose + gripper + mobile-base motion + discrete control-mode selector, i.e. mixed (re-confirmed unchanged, now with a more direct/official source than before).; action_frame=CORRECTED from 'both' to 'delta'. Fetched robocasa/scripts/dataset_scripts/convert_hdf5_lerobot.py directly from GitHub main: the absolute-action computation is present in source but COMMENTED OUT ('# action_abs = env.base_env.convert_rel_to_abs_action(actions[t])', '# traj["actions_abs"].append(...)'), and the LeRobot feature schema written to disk defines only a single 'action' key (shape (12,)) with no action_abs/actions_abs key -- the official released dataset ships only the delta/relative action (per robosuite OSC_POSE default: 'delta values from the current state'). The previous 'both' classification relied on a third-party HF mirror (Asap7772/robocasa-mimicgen-PnPCounterToCab) of an older/different processing pipeline that did include action_abs; that is not representative of the current official conversion path.; rotation_representation=robosuite OSC_POSE controller docs (robosuite.ai/docs/modules/controllers.html, fetched directly): 'delta rotations from the current end-effector orientation in the form of axis-angle coordinates (ax, ay, az)'. name: RoboCook
field_sources: source_url=Verified live via curl against https://hshi74.github.io/robocook/ (official project page for the CoRL 2023 Best System Paper Award RoboCook work); loads and links to [Paper]/[Code]/[Data]. Stub value confirmed correct, unchanged.; paper_url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.14447 -- "RoboCook: Long-Horizon Elasto-Plastic Object Manipulation with Diverse Tools", Shi, Xu, Clarke, Li, Wu, Stanford University/UIUC, CoRL 2023 Best System Paper Award. Linked directly from the project page's [Paper] button.; license=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hshi74/robocook/main/LICENSE ("MIT License, Copyright (c) 2023 Haochen Shi"). Caveat: this is the license on the GitHub code repository; no separate, explicit license statement was found for the real-world dataset itself (shared via an unlicensed Google Drive folder linked from the README), so MIT is recorded as the best available evidence rather than a data-specific license grant.; raw_format=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hshi74/robocook/main/README.md "Data" section: "raw: because the raw ROSbag data are huge, we share an episode of random exploration ... as a sample." The underlying real-world sensor capture format is ROS bag. Caveat: only one small sample episode of the raw ROSbag data is actually shared publicly (full raw capture was not released due to size); the bulk of what is downloadable is derived/processed data (per-frame .h5 files for the "dynamics" dataset, .ply point clouds for "tool_classification").; release_type=Project shares a static, pre-collected/pre-processed real-world dataset (raw sample + dynamics/tool_classification/planning subsets on Google Drive per README) plus the RoboCook code framework used to produce it -- not a procedural generation framework, scene/asset platform, or standalone RL benchmark env, so fixed_episode_dataset fits best.; collection_method=arXiv:2306.14447 PDF Sec 6.2.1 "Data Collection": "we collect around 20 minutes of data for each tool using a behavior policy that randomly samples parameters within a predefined action space. In each episode, the robot applies multiple action sequences to the soft object, and after the current episode, a human manually resets the environment." This is autonomous, scripted random-exploration data collection (no human teleoperation of the arm); the human's role is limited to manually reshaping/resetting the dough between episodes, not driving the robot.; secondary_collection_methods=No teleoperation, UMI, egocentric-human, or simulation data collection is described anywhere in arXiv:2306.14447 or the GitHub README -- all real-world data collection (dynamics, tool classification) uses the same random-exploration behavior policy / pre-coded dumpling pipeline. Left empty.; is_multi_embodiment=arXiv:2306.14447 PDF Sec 6.5.1: single "7-DoF Franka Emika Panda robot arm and its parallel jaw gripper as the base robot" used throughout all experiments and data collection. Single, standardized embodiment.; embodiment_class=arXiv:2306.14447 PDF Sec 6.5.1 -- single fixed-base Franka Panda arm setup, no second arm, no mobile base, no humanoid/hand tracking.; robot_platform=arXiv:2306.14447 PDF Sec 6.5.1: "We use the 7-DoF Franka Emika Panda robot arm and its parallel jaw gripper as the base robot."; num_arms=arXiv:2306.14447 PDF Sec 6.5.1 and project page hardware photo (Figure 4) show exactly one robot arm.; dof_per_arm=arXiv:2306.14447 PDF Sec 6.5.1: "We use the 7-DoF Franka Emika Panda robot arm..."; gripper_type=arXiv:2306.14447 PDF Sec 6.5.1: "...and its parallel jaw gripper as the base robot." Note: many of the 14-15 3D-printed tools (rollers, presses, grippers, knife, spatulas, etc., Sec 6.5.2/6.5.3) attach to and are actuated by this same parallel-jaw gripper via a quick-connector mechanism, rather than replacing it with a different end-effector type.; hand_pose_representation=Derived -- the end effector is the Franka''s standard 2-finger parallel-jaw gripper (see gripper_type), not an articulated/dexterous hand or bare-hand tracking, so no MANO/keypoint/joint-angle finger-shape encoding applies. HandPoseRepresentation.NONE.; has_mobile_base=arXiv:2306.14447 PDF Sec 6.5.1/Figure 4 -- fixed tabletop Franka arm bolted next to a stationary workspace with fixed tool racks; no mobile base anywhere in the setup.; action_space=arXiv:2306.14447 PDF Sec 3.2/Figure 3(B): the parametrized action spaces are Cartesian/tool-pose based, e.g. gripping a=(r, theta, d) (rod separation, rotation angle, depth) and pressing/rolling a=(x, y, z, theta) (tool position + rotation angle) -- these are end-effector/tool-pose displacement parameters, not joint-space commands, so eef_pose is the closest fit. Note action_dim is intentionally left blank below because it varies by tool (3 for gripping, 4 for pressing/rolling) rather than being a single fixed value across the whole dataset.; action_frame=Left blank: the paper (arXiv:2306.14447 Sec 3.2/6.4) defines each tool's action as bounded Cartesian/rotation parameters (e.g. a=(x,y,z,theta)) but never explicitly states whether these parameters are absolute world-frame targets or relative/delta displacements from the tool's current pose -- no citable statement found either way, so left blank rather than guessed.; rotation_representation=Left blank: action rotation components are a single scalar angle theta (e.g. a=(x,y,z,theta) for pressing/rolling, a=(r,theta,d) for gripping; arXiv:2306.14447 Figure 3(B)), representing rotation about one axis only. This does not cleanly match any existing RotationRepresentation enum value (euler_xyz/quaternion/rotation_6d/axis_angle/rotation_matrix all describe full 3D orientation, not a single scalar angle), so left blank with a suggested_new_enum_values entry instead of forcing an imprecise match.; state_dim=Left blank: RoboCook's "state" is a processed point cloud (300 sampled surface points, arXiv:2306.14447 Sec 6.2/Figure 2) rather than a fixed-length proprioceptive vector, so a single scalar state_dim does not meaningfully apply.; action_dim=Left blank: action dimensionality varies by tool -- 3 for gripping (r, theta, d) vs. 4 for pressing/rolling (x, y, z, theta) per arXiv:2306.14447 Figure 3(B) -- there is no single fixed action_dim across the whole dataset.; fps=arXiv:2306.14447 PDF Sec 6.5.1: "Four calibrated Intel RealSense D415 RGB-D cameras ... capture 1280x720 RGB-D images at 30 Hz."; fps_variable=Single fixed 30 Hz camera capture rate stated in arXiv:2306.14447 Sec 6.5.1, no mention of a variable rate anywhere in the paper or README.; num_camera_views=arXiv:2306.14447 PDF Sec 6.5.1: "Four calibrated Intel RealSense D415 RGB-D cameras are fixed on vertical metal bars around the robot tabletop" (also depicted as 4 dashed white circles at the four corners of the table in Figure 4).; camera_views=arXiv:2306.14447 Sec 6.5.1/Figure 4 -- all four RealSense D415 cameras are static, table-external, exterior-facing units mounted around the workspace perimeter (no wrist-mounted, head-mounted, or body-worn camera), so mapped to the single third_person category.; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=arXiv:2306.14447 Sec 6.2/Figure 2: the four calibrated camera point clouds are merged into one unified scene point cloud per perception timestep ("the input to the perception module is a raw observation point cloud merged from four RGBD cameras"), implying frame-synchronized capture across the rig.; has_camera_calibration=arXiv:2306.14447 Sec 6.5.1: "Four calibrated Intel RealSense D415 RGB-D cameras..." -- explicitly described as calibrated.; depth_coverage=arXiv:2306.14447 Sec 6.2 -- the RGB-D depth from all four cameras is used to reconstruct a full watertight mesh/point cloud of the dough and workspace (crop ROI, extract dough point cloud, reconstruct watertight mesh, sample surface points), i.e. full depth coverage of the manipulation region, not partial/none.; additional_modalities=Checked arXiv:2306.14447 (full PDF text) and the GitHub README for force/torque, tactile, audio, or eye-gaze sensing: Sec 6.5.1's hardware list is only the Franka arm + parallel gripper + 4 RealSense D415 RGB-D cameras + 3D-printed tools; no dedicated force-torque sensor, tactile sensor, microphone, or eye-tracking device is mentioned anywhere despite the tools" varied contact-rich interactions. Left empty rather than assuming sensing that is not documented.; has_language_instruction=Checked arXiv:2306.14447 (full PDF text) and the GitHub README for any natural-language instruction/annotation field -- none found; tasks/subgoals are specified via target point-cloud configurations (goal-conditioned), not free-form language strings.; num_task_types=arXiv:2306.14447 abstract/Sec 1: "a general-purpose robot arm can learn complex long-horizon soft object manipulation tasks, such as making dumplings and alphabet letter cookies" -- 2 distinct long-horizon composite tasks are demonstrated end-to-end (dumpling-making; alphabet-letter-cookie-shaping, covering letters R/O/B/C/K). Distinct from the 14-15 individual tool-use primitives (Sec 6.5.2), which are sub-skills composed into these 2 task types, not separate task types themselves.; urdf_available=Following the precedent set for other Franka-Panda-based configs in this registry (e.g. droid.yaml, furniturebench.yaml): the manufacturer's official Franka Panda URDF is published in https://github.com/frankaemika/franka_ros (franka_description/robots/panda/panda.urdf.xacro), applicable to RoboCook's robot_platform=franka_panda. Note: no URDF for RoboCook's custom 3D-printed tools was found -- only tool mesh files are shared via the Google Drive link in the README ("we also share the 3D models of all the tools"), format unconfirmed (likely STL for 3D printing, not URDF).; urdf_source=Franka Panda URDF is not vendored inside the hshi74/robocook GitHub repository itself; it is sourced from the manufacturer''s official franka_ros package (frankaemika/franka_ros), so manufacturer_official.; num_scenes=arXiv:2306.14447 Sec 6.5.1/Figure 4: a single fixed lab tabletop workspace with fixed camera rig and tool racks is used throughout; no scene diversity (multiple rooms/tables/lighting setups) is described.; num_objects=arXiv:2306.14447 -- all tasks manipulate a single class of manipulandum, elasto-plastic dough (Sec 1 abstract: "manipulates elasto-plastic objects with various tools"); the 14-15 3D-printed tools (Sec 6.5.2) are end-effector attachments, not separate manipulated objects, so num_objects=1 (dough) rather than counting tools.
suggested_new_enum_values: rotation_representation=single_axis_angle -- RoboCook's action space parametrizes tool rotation as one scalar angle theta about a single (vertical) axis (arXiv:2306.14447 Figure 3(B): a=(x,y,z,theta) for pressing/rolling, a=(r,theta,d) for gripping), which is not represented by any current RotationRepresentation value (euler_xyz/quaternion/rotation_6d/axis_angle/rotation_matrix all encode full 3D orientation, not a single scalar angle).

collection_method=robogen-ai.github.io and arXiv:2311.01455 (tasks, scenes and skills are proposed/generated/solved entirely inside a PyBullet-based physics simulator; no teleop or real robot); secondary_collection_methods=readme.md 'Learn skills' section + execute.py/execute_locomotion.py: substeps are solved autonomously via RL (SAC/Ray-RLlib), motion-planning primitives (OMPL), or trajectory optimization/CEM -- no human teleoperation found anywhere in the repo (grep for 'teleop' returns nothing) -- so autonomous_policy is a fitting secondary method alongside simulation; is_multi_embodiment=github.com/Genesis-Embodied-AI/RoboGen repo layout: manipulation/ (panda.py/sawyer.py/ur5.py single-arm robots) and locomotion/ subfolders a1/, anymal/ (quadrupeds) and atlas/ (humanoid) are separate, roughly co-equal modules; embodiment_class=Left blank on this re-verification pass (previously set to single_arm). manipulation/ covers single_arm robots while locomotion/a1, locomotion/anymal (quadruped) and locomotion/atlas (humanoid) are separate co-equal modules with no single representative embodiment; forcing one value would misrepresent the multi-embodiment framework (see suggested_new_enum_values for a possible mixed/composite value); robot_platform=arXiv:2311.01455 methodology section explicitly frames the manipulation module around Franka ('we explain details of RoboGen in the context of a robotic arm (e.g., Franka)'; GPT-4 prompts say 'You can think of the robotic arm as a Franka Panda robot'). Note manipulation/sim.py load_robot() actually randomly samples panda/sawyer/ur5 at runtime (manipulation/utils.py default_config has no fixed robot_name), and locomotion/ targets Unitree A1, ANYmal and Atlas which have no robot_platform enum entry -- franka_panda is kept as the paper's canonical illustrative default, see suggested_new_enum_values; num_arms=manipulation/panda.py (single right_end_effector arm; right_arm_joint_indices has 7 entries); dof_per_arm=manipulation/panda.py (right_arm_joint_indices = [0,1,2,3,4,5,6], 7 controllable arm joints); gripper_type=CORRECTED from parallel_jaw to suction. manipulation/utils.py default_config sets use_suction: True (the default used to load every example task, none of the 95 example_tasks/*.yaml override it); manipulation/sim.py grasp_action_mag = 0.06 if not use_suction else 1, and activate_suction()/deactivate_suction() create a pybullet constraint at the gripper-object contact point when action[6] >= 0. The physical Franka/Sawyer/UR5 gripper mesh has 2 actuated finger joints (panda.py right_gripper_indices), but the DEFAULT simulated grasping behavior used across the released code/examples is the suction abstraction, not finger actuation; hand_pose_representation=New field, filled none. The end effector is either the suction abstraction or a 2-finger parallel gripper (see gripper_type); no dexterous/articulated hand or bare-hand tracking is used anywhere in the manipulation or locomotion modules; has_mobile_base=manipulation/sim.py load_robot() calls self.robot.init(..., fixed_base=True, ...) -- fixed tabletop manipulation setup in the manipulation module (locomotion module legged robots are categorized as quadruped/humanoid embodiment, not a wheeled/tracked mobile base); action_space=manipulation/sim.py (self.action_low/self.action_high are 7-dim: delta end-effector translation+rotation plus a suction/gripper action); action_frame=manipulation/sim.py (translation_mode default is 'delta-translation'); rotation_representation=manipulation/sim.py / manipulation/utils.py default_config (rotation_mode default is 'delta-axis-angle-local'); action_dim=manipulation/sim.py (7-element action_low/action_high arrays: 3 translation + 3 rotation + 1 suction/gripper); fps_variable=manipulation/sim.py (dt=0.01, frameskip=2 defaults, both user-configurable constructor params) and locomotion/sim.py (dt=0.01, frameskip=10 defaults) give different effective control rates per module/config; GIF/MP4 exports additionally use their own fixed export fps (10/60) unrelated to the sim control rate -- no single fixed dataset-wide fps; num_camera_views=manipulation/sim.py and locomotion/sim.py both call setup_camera()/setup_camera_rpy() exactly once, configuring a single fixed external render viewpoint; camera_views=manipulation/sim.py and locomotion/sim.py (single fixed external/third-person viewpoint defined by camera_eye/camera_target or yaw-pitch-roll, not head- or wrist-mounted); has_synchronized_multiview_rig=New field, filled false. Only one camera viewpoint is ever configured per env (see num_camera_views/camera_views sources) -- no multi-camera synchronized rig; has_camera_calibration=manipulation/sim.py (camera pose/FOV are hardcoded constructor constants, not exported as per-episode calibration files); depth_coverage=manipulation/sim.py and locomotion/sim.py render() both return rgb img and depth from p.getCameraImage on every call; additional_modalities=Checked manipulation/{sim,panda,sawyer,ur5,robot}.py and locomotion/sim.py for force/torque sensing, tactile, audio, or eye-gaze -- none found; observations are limited to rgb/depth images and simulator joint/pose state; has_language_instruction=example_tasks/ task_config yaml files contain GPT-4-generated task_name/task_description natural-language fields, e.g. Change_Lamp_Direction example (verified via GitHub raw file); urdf_available=readme.md Dataset section: a parsed PartNet-Mobility URDF dataset is provided via a Google Drive download link; urdf_source=readme.md (object URDFs come from PartNet-Mobility, a third-party academic asset collection accessed via sapien.ucsd.edu, plus Objaverse assets; not authored in this repo nor official manufacturer CAD); source_url=https://robogen-ai.github.io/ (verified HTTP 200; matches the official project page linked from arXiv:2311.01455 and the GitHub repo README); paper_url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01455 (verified HTTP 200; RoboGen: Towards Unleashing Infinite Data for Automated Robot Learning via Generative Simulation, ICML 2024)
suggested_new_enum_values: robot_platform=unitree_a1, anymal, atlas -- RoboGen's locomotion module (locomotion/a1, locomotion/anymal, locomotion/atlas) targets these three legged/humanoid robots, none of which map to an existing robot_platform value (unitree_g1/unitree_h1 are different bipedal robots); embodiment_class=no single new literal proposed; RoboGen is a case where is_multi_embodiment=true but no embodiment is clearly primary (single_arm manipulation vs. quadruped/humanoid locomotion modules are co-equal).
