suggested_new_enum_values: embodiment_class=multi_embodiment (or similar) -- RoboMIND deliberately spans 4 heterogeneous platforms at once within one collection: single_arm (Franka Emika Panda, UR5e), dual_arm (AgileX Cobot Magic V2.0), and humanoid (Tien Kung with dual dexterous hands). None of the existing single-value options (single_arm/dual_arm/humanoid/mobile_manipulator/human_hand) correctly describes the collection as a whole, so the field was left blank instead of arbitrarily picking one embodiment. Also left robot_platform blank for the same reason.; gripper_type=mixed -- 3 of the 4 embodiments (Franka, UR5e, AgileX) use Robotiq parallel-jaw grippers while the Tien Kung humanoid uses Inspire-Robots RH56DFX dexterous hands (per arXiv:2412.13877 Sec III.A / Sec V.A). The dataset as a whole therefore mixes parallel_jaw and dexterous_hand end-effectors and doesn't fit either single existing enum value; a 'mixed' option analogous to ActionSpace.MIXED would let this be represented without forcing a wrong single choice. Also left num_arms and dof_per_arm blank for the analogous reason (1 vs 2 arms, 6 vs 7 DoF depending on platform).

name: RoboNet
field_sources: source_url=Stub recorded a TensorFlow-Datasets mirror page (tensorflow.google.cn/datasets/catalog/robonet). Corrected to the dataset's own canonical project webpage http://www.robonet.wiki/, which is the site cited as 'the project webpage' throughout the paper (arXiv:1910.11215, footnotes 1 and 3) and linked from the GitHub repo README (https://github.com/SudeepDasari/RoboNet/blob/master/README.md); license=https://github.com/SudeepDasari/RoboNet/blob/master/README.md: 'All data is provided under the Creative Commons BY 4.0 license.' Confirmed by the presence of a separate LICENSE_DATASET file in the repo root (https://github.com/SudeepDasari/RoboNet); raw_format=GitHub wiki 'Getting Started' page (https://github.com/SudeepDasari/RoboNet/wiki/Getting-Started) and repo code (robonet/datasets/util/hdf5_loader.py, robonet/datasets/robonet_dataset.py) load the dataset from a folder of .hdf5 files via h5py, with per-trajectory RGB frames stored as mp4/jpg-encoded groups (env/cam{i}_video) inside each hdf5 file, plus env/state and policy/actions arrays; collection_method=arXiv:1910.11215 sec 4.1 'Data Collection Process': 'the dataset is collected autonomously with minimal human intervention, in a self-supervised manner' and 'trajectories are collected by applying actions drawn at random from simple hand-engineered distributions. We most commonly use a diagonal Gaussian combined [with] the automatic grasping primitive'; gripper_type=arXiv:1910.11215 Table 1 lists gripper types used: Weiss Robotics WSG-50, Robotiq, WidowX, Baxter, Franka, and Kuka stock grippers — all of these are standard two-finger parallel-jaw end-effectors (WSG-50 and Robotiq 2-finger grippers, and the stock two-finger grippers shipped with the WidowX/Baxter/Franka Panda/Kuka LBR iiwa arms), none are suction, dexterous/multi-finger hands, or bare arms; action_space=arXiv:1910.11215 sec 4.1: 'All trajectories in RoboNet share a similar action space, which consists of deltas in position and rotation to the robot end-effector, with one additional dimension of the action vector reserved for the gripper joint... We chose an action parametrization in end-effector space rather than joint-space'; action_frame=arXiv:1910.11215 sec 4.1: 'the action space...consists of deltas in position and rotation to the robot end-effector' — explicitly a delta/relative action, not absolute joint or pose commands; camera_views=arXiv:1910.11215 Table 1 ('Camera configuration: 113') and sec 5.2 ('we attempt...tasks from two views...compare a model trained on 90 different viewpoints...The arrangement of the cameras is shown in Appendix D') describe many distinct external camera placements/angles around the workspace; the paper and repo code (ncam-indexed env/cam{i}_video groups) never mention any robot-mounted/wrist camera, so all camera views are external third-person viewpoints, just varying in position/angle across the 113 configurations; has_camera_calibration=arXiv:1910.11215 sec 4.1: 'The frame of reference is the root link of the robot, which need not coincide with the camera pose. This avoids the need to calibrate the camera, but requires any model to infer the relative positioning between the camera and the robots' reference frames from a history of context frames.' — explicitly states cameras are uncalibrated; depth_coverage=arXiv:1910.11215 sec 4.2: 'In theory, one could add any type (depth, tactile, audio, etc.) of sensor data to RoboNet, but we stick to consumer RGB video cameras for the purposes of this project.' — no depth sensing is collected; has_language_instruction=No language/task annotations are mentioned anywhere in arXiv:1910.11215 or the RoboNet repo/wiki (https://github.com/SudeepDasari/RoboNet); data is collected via undirected random/autonomous exploration (sec 4.1) with only image, state, and action tensors stored per trajectory (robonet/datasets/util/hdf5_loader.py), with no text/task field in the hdf5 schema; urdf_available=https://github.com/SudeepDasari/RoboNet top-level repo contents (.gitignore, LICENSE, LICENSE_DATASET, README.md, launch_configs, requirements.txt, robonet, robonet_experiments, scripts, setup.py) contain no URDF files or URDF-related directory, and none of the wiki pages reference URDFs; urdf_source=Same as urdf_available — no URDF files found in the dataset repo (https://github.com/SudeepDasari/RoboNet) or wiki; expected_size_gb=GitHub wiki 'Getting Started' page (https://github.com/SudeepDasari/RoboNet/wiki/Getting-Started): 'RoboNet is a large dataset: currently it is a 36GB download' (referring to the robonet_v3.tar.gz full release); expected_num_episodes=arXiv:1910.11215 abstract and sec 4.2: 'a dataset containing roughly 162,000 trajectories...from 7 robots'; Table 1 breakdown sums to ~161.7k (Sawyer 68k + Baxter 18k + WidowX 5k + Franka 7.9k + Kuka 1.8k + Fetch 5k + GoogleRobot 56k); paper_url=Cited throughout repo/wiki as 'the RoboNet paper'; CoRL 2019 paper, Dasari et al. 'RoboNet: Large-Scale Multi-Robot Learning', arXiv:1910.11215.; is_multi_embodiment=arXiv:1910.11215 abstract + Table 1: dataset combines 7 distinct robot platforms (Sawyer, Baxter, WidowX, Franka, Kuka, Fetch, GoogleRobot) from 4 institutions -- an intentional multi-robot collection, not single-embodiment.; has_mobile_base=arXiv:1910.11215 Appendix B.1: state/action space for all 7 robots is restricted to end-effector XYZ + yaw + gripper joint; no base-motion dimension defined for any robot, and all tasks are stationary tabletop object-relocation tasks.; hand_pose_representation=Table 1 lists only 2-finger parallel-jaw grippers (WSG-50, Robotiq, WidowX/Baxter/Franka/Kuka stock grippers); Appendix B.1 records only a single binarized gripper joint-angle value, no dexterous-hand or bare-hand pose data -- 'none' applies.; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=GitHub wiki Getting-Started page (github.com/SudeepDasari/RoboNet/wiki/Getting-Started) TF-loading example shows image batches shaped (B, T, N_VIEWS, H, W, C) -- multiple camera views recorded together per trajectory in the hdf5 files (env/cam{i}_video groups).
suggested_new_enum_values: robot_platform=RoboNet is an intentionally multi-embodiment collection spanning 7 distinct robot platforms (Sawyer, Baxter, WidowX, Franka Panda, Kuka LBR iiwa, Fetch, and a Google robot arm — arXiv:1910.11215 Table 1), several of which (baxter, kuka_lbr_iiwa, fetch, google_robot) have no matching value in the current single-select robot_platform enum, and the field itself has no 'multi_platform'/'heterogeneous' option to represent a dataset spanning many robots at once. Left blank here rather than forcing one dominant robot (e.g. 'sawyer', which is only ~42% of trajectories) or the lossy 'other' catch-all.; embodiment_class=6 of the 7 constituent robots (Sawyer, WidowX, Franka, Kuka, Fetch, GoogleRobot) are single_arm, but Baxter (~18k/162k trajectories, ~11%) is a dual-arm platform, so no single embodiment_class value accurately describes the whole collection; a 'mixed'/'multi_embodiment' enum value would let per-source-heterogeneous collections like RoboNet be tagged honestly instead of leaving the field blank.; num_arms=Same heterogeneity as embodiment_class: Baxter contributes 2-arm data while the other 6 platforms are single-arm, so no single integer value is accurate for the collection as a whole.; dof_per_arm=DoF varies by constituent robot (e.g. 7-DoF Sawyer/Franka/Kuka/Baxter arms vs. the lower-cost WidowX arm, which has fewer joints), so no single integer accurately represents the whole multi-robot collection.; state_dim / action_dim=Per arXiv:1910.11215 sec 4.1, 'The action space can also be a subset of the listed dimensions' — state and action dimensionality (sdim/adim in the dataset's own metadata schema) genuinely varies per constituent robot/source file rather than being fixed dataset-wide, so no single state_dim/action_dim integer is accurate for the collection as a whole.; rotation_representation=Most RoboNet robots (excluding Google R3) restrict orientation to a single yaw angle (roll/pitch locked, gripper always pointing downward) per arXiv:1910.11215 Appendix B.1's R5 state definition (XYZ + yaw + gripper). This is not a full 3-axis euler_xyz, quaternion, 6D, or axis_angle representation; left blank rather than forcing a full-orientation enum value. A 'yaw_only'/'single_axis_angle' enum option would represent this restricted-rotation convention precisely.

name: RoboOmni
field_sources: source_url=HF dataset search API https://huggingface.co/api/datasets?search=OmniAction resolved OpenMOSS-Team/OmniAction as the actual repo (stub had a pasted page title, not a URL); dataset README also mirrors this at https://huggingface.co/datasets/fnlp/OmniAction and https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/OmniAction; license=HF dataset card metadata (license: cc-by-nc-4.0) at https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/OmniAction; raw_format=Dataset README states 'Format: RLDS (Reinforcement Learning Datasets standard)'; repo file listing confirms .tfrecord shards (RLDS is stored as TFRecord) at https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/OmniAction; collection_method=Re-verified: paper Sec 3.2 'Construction Process' / 'Textual Scripting' step: 'We sample tasks and trajectories from Open-X Embodiment datasets (Padalkar et al., 2023)' and filter 74,645 base trajectories -> expanded into 141,162 episodes (App A.1). The underlying OXE subsets (Bridge/WidowX, Fractal/Google-robot, Jaco Play) were originally collected via human teleoperation; OmniAction only adds synthetic audio/dialogue on top, it does not recollect robot motion. arXiv:2510.23763 Sec 3.2, App A.1.; embodiment_class=Re-verified: all three source subsets (Bridge-WidowX, Fractal/Google-robot, Jaco Play) drive a single 7-D end-effector action stream with no base terms (arXiv:2510.23763 Sec 3.1), so 'single_arm' fits the action space used here. Caveat: the Fractal/Google-robot platform is physically mounted on a mobile base in other literature (it is *not* actuated/represented in OmniAction's action vector), so this is a simplification for a multi-platform dataset -- see suggested_new_enum_values for embodiment_class.; num_arms=Same as embodiment_class basis - each source subset controls exactly one arm.; action_space=Paper Sec. 3.1: 'a_t denotes the delta control vector of the end-effector' -> eef_pose control, confirmed by Fig.4 notation Δx, Δθ, ΔGrip (arXiv:2510.23763).; action_frame=Paper Sec. 3.1 explicitly: 'a_t denotes the delta control vector of the end-effector' (arXiv:2510.23763).; rotation_representation=Re-verified: paper text confirms a_t in R^7 = delta eef pose + gripper (Sec 3.1) but does not explicitly spell out the rotation encoding in extracted text (a figure notation cited in an earlier pass could not be re-confirmed from the PDF's extracted text layer). 'euler_xyz' is kept as a reasoned inference from the standard OXE 7-D convention (dx,dy,dz,d-roll,d-pitch,d-yaw,gripper) used by Bridge/RT-1/Jaco Play, not a direct quote -- flagged as lower-confidence than other fields.; action_dim=Paper Sec. 3.1: 'a_t ∈ R^7' and Sec 4.1: 'FAST+ ... a continuous action vector a_t ∈ R^7 (e.g., 7-DoF control)' (arXiv:2510.23763).; has_mobile_base=Re-verified: no base-motion dimension appears in the 7-D action vector for any of the three source subsets (arXiv:2510.23763 Sec 3.1). Caveat: the Fractal/Google-robot platform's physical chassis has a mobile base in other sources, but it is not actuated/represented anywhere in OmniAction's data, so 'false' describes the dataset's action space, not necessarily every source robot's full hardware.; has_language_instruction=Paper Sec 3.1: each sample is a triplet (C, I, A) where C is a multi-turn conversation (user turns as audio, assistant turns as text) that ultimately drives the action; instructions/dialogue are core to every episode. arXiv:2510.23763.; num_task_types=Paper Sec 3.1/Fig. 11: OmniAction 'spans 112 skills (e.g., pick-place, open/close) and 748 objects' - taken as the count of distinct manipulation task/skill types. arXiv:2510.23763.; urdf_available=No URDF or robot-description files appear in the HF dataset repo file listing (only README.md, .gitattributes, and per-subset .tfrecord shards) at https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/OmniAction?full=true.; urdf_source=Same as urdf_available - no URDF files found in the dataset repo.; expected_num_episodes=Re-verified: HF README ('It comprises 141,162 episodes...') and paper App A.1 ('74,645 base trajectories ... expanded into 141,162 multimodal episodes') both state 141,162; matches prior value. arXiv:2510.23763.; expected_size_gb=Re-verified this session via HF Hub API https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/OmniAction?full=true: usedStorage = 2,710,899,824,323 bytes ~= 2710.9 GB (decimal), matches prior value.; paper_url=HF dataset card links arXiv paper (accepted ICLR 2026); README lists 'arXiv Paper' -> https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.23763, abs page https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.23763.; is_multi_embodiment=HF repo file listing (api/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/OmniAction?full=true) shows top-level shard prefixes bridge_*, fractal_*, jaco_play_* -- three distinct OXE source platforms (WidowX/Bridge, Google-robot/Fractal, Kinova Jaco/Jaco Play) combined in one release; paper Sec 3.2 confirms sampling 'from Open-X Embodiment datasets' generally.; additional_modalities=Paper abstract/Sec 3.1: dataset centers on synthesized audio -- 5,096 speaker timbres, 2,482 non-verbal sound events, 640 environmental background soundscapes, all mixed into the audio channel alongside vision; HF card tags include 'audio-to-audio'. arXiv:2510.23763.; hand_pose_representation=Action space is a scalar gripper term (Sec 3.1: a_t in R^7 = eef delta pose + 1D gripper), not a dexterous/hand-shape encoding (no MANO/keypoints/joint-angle hand model referenced anywhere); 'none' fits per schema description. arXiv:2510.23763 Sec 3.1.; num_objects=Paper Sec 3.1/App A.1 and HF README both state OmniAction spans '112 skills ... and 748 objects' (748 manipulable objects, e.g. 'can'); Fig. 11. arXiv:2510.23763.; release_type=OmniAction is released as a static collection of 141,162 pre-generated episodes (tfrecord shards on HF), not a generation framework/scene platform/RL env -- 'fixed_episode_dataset' fits. Note: paper also introduces a companion 'OmniAction-LIBERO' simulation benchmark variant (Sec 3.3), which is a separate resource not covered by this source_url.; secondary_collection_methods=Investigated but left empty: the OmniAction construction pipeline (textual scripting via GPT-4o + TTS-based 'auditory realization' of speech/sound events/backgrounds, Sec 3.2) is a synthetic multimodal-annotation overlay on pre-existing teleop trajectories, not a second robot-motion collection method: none of the current CollectionMethod enum values describe this pattern. See suggested_new_enum_values.; num_subjects=Investigated but left blank: paper states '5,096 distinct speaker timbres' (App A.1, README), but these are synthetic TTS voices generated via MOSS-TTSD/CosyVoice/Gemini-TTS with voice cloning (Sec 3.2 'Auditory Realization'), not physical human subjects/demonstrators -- does not match num_subjects' intended meaning, so left blank rather than mapping loosely.; num_scenes=Investigated but left blank: paper states '640 environmental backgrounds' (App A.1), but these are ambient audio soundscapes (e.g. running water, stir-fry sizzling) mixed at controlled SNR (Sec 3.2), not distinct physical task environments/rooms -- does not match num_scenes' intended meaning, so left blank.; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=Investigated: neither the HF README, dataset card, nor the paper text (extracted from PDF) describe the camera rig/viewpoint setup used per episode; no evidence found, left blank.; camera_views=Investigated: no explicit camera-view description found in the paper text or HF README for the repackaged OmniAction release; the underlying OXE subsets have known camera setups individually, but OmniAction's own documentation does not restate them, so left blank rather than guessing per sub-dataset.; dof_per_hand=Not applicable / no evidence: dataset uses standard parallel/2-finger grippers via a scalar gripper action term (Sec 3.1), not a dexterous multi-DoF hand; left blank.; expected_duration_hours=Investigated: no total dataset duration/hours statistic found in the paper or README (only per-clip audio-segment-length stats in Fig. 10b, '10 to 80 seconds' typical clip length, which is not a dataset-total duration); left blank.
suggested_new_enum_values: robot_platform=OmniAction re-purposes trajectories from three distinct Open-X-Embodiment robot platforms (WidowX/Bridge, Google-robot/Fractal aka RT-1 robot, and Kinova Jaco/Jaco Play) mixed together in one dataset. None of these exactly match a single existing enum value ('widowx' only covers one of the three, and there is no 'google_robot'/'kinova_jaco' option), so no single robot_platform value accurately represents the whole dataset. Proposal: add 'google_robot' and 'kinova_jaco' as robot_platform options, plus a 'mixed' value for datasets that combine multiple source-dataset embodiments like this one, rather than forcing 'other' which loses the multi-embodiment detail.; gripper_type=The action vector's gripper term (ΔGrip) is a single scalar per source subset, but the three underlying platforms use different physical end-effectors (WidowX parallel-jaw gripper, Google-robot/RT-1 two-finger gripper, Kinova Jaco's factory 3-finger hand) - could not confirm a single uniform gripper_type across the whole mixed dataset from available sources, so left this field blank rather than guessing.; embodiment_class=OmniAction mixes 3 OXE source platforms; two (WidowX/Bridge, Kinova Jaco/Jaco Play) are stationary single-arm rigs, but the third (Google-robot/Fractal) is physically a mobile-manipulator chassis elsewhere in the literature even though its base is not actuated in this dataset's 7-D action vector. No single EmbodimentClass value cleanly covers a dataset built from a mix of stationary-arm and mobile-manipulator source platforms; propose adding a 'mixed' value for multi-embodiment datasets like this one, similar to the robot_platform suggestion below.; collection_method=OmniAction's defining construction step is not a robot-motion collection method at all -- it is a synthetic multimodal annotation overlay (GPT-4o dialogue scripting + multi-engine TTS speech/sound-event/background audio synthesis, Sec 3.2) applied on top of pre-existing teleop trajectories sampled from Open-X Embodiment. None of the current CollectionMethod values (teleop/autonomous_policy/umi/egocentric_human/simulation/human_to_robot_synthesis/ar_haptic_guided_synthesis/scene_asset_curation) describe 'synthetic audio/instruction augmentation of an existing dataset'. Propose adding e.g. 'synthetic_multimodal_augmentation' as a secondary_collection_methods option for this pattern.

name: RoboSet
field_sources: license=robopen.github.io/roboset/ page footer states: 'This work is licensed under the MIT-License'; confirmed in github.com/robopen/roboagent README License section ('The RoboAgent code and RoboSet datasets are both licensed under MIT License').; raw_format=Re-verified: arXiv:2309.01918 Appendix A: 'The data was collected ... and saved in HDF5 format.' robopen.github.io/roboset/ code snippet loads trials via h5py.File(...).; embodiment_class=arXiv:2309.01918 (RoboAgent paper) Section 4 / Appendix B.1: single fixed-base Franka Emika Panda arm in a table-top kitchen setup, no mobile base described.; robot_platform=arXiv:2309.01918 Section 4: 'a Franka Emika Panda arm with a two-finger Robotiq gripper'; github.com/robopen/roboagent README: 'evaluating on Franka Panda arms'.; num_arms=arXiv:2309.01918 describes a single Franka Panda arm throughout the RoboSet/RoboAgent system.; dof_per_arm=arXiv:2309.01918 Appendix B.1: action space is '8 (7 joint positions, 1 dimension for end-effector open/close)', i.e. the standard 7-DOF Franka Panda arm.; gripper_type=arXiv:2309.01918 Section 4: 'two-finger Robotiq gripper fitted with Festo Adaptive Fingers' (Robotiq 2F-85/140 is a parallel-jaw gripper). Note: a separate, much larger ~70,000-trajectory autonomous bin-picking release described in the same paper's Appendix A footnote and on robopen.github.io/roboset/autonomous.html includes some subsets (e.g. Set 13/15/16, 'D'Manus hand') using a dexterous-hand end-effector instead; that release is not counted in this config's episode/field values, which describe the core teleop+kinesthetic RoboSet.; has_mobile_base=arXiv:2309.01918 Section 4: fixed table-top/kitchen setup with a stationary Franka arm; no mobile base is mentioned anywhere in the paper or project site.; action_space=arXiv:2309.01918 Appendix B.1: 'The robot ... is operated with joint position control, with an action space dimension of 8 (7 joint positions, 1 dimension for end-effector open/close)'.; rotation_representation=arXiv:2309.01918 Appendix B.1: the 8-dim action space is pure joint-position + gripper; no explicit end-effector orientation/rotation representation is used for actions.; state_dim=CORRECTED 14->8. robopen.github.io/roboset/ Data Schema image: qp_arm float[7] (arm joint pos) + qp_ee float[1] (Robotiq gripper pos) = 8, mirroring action_dim (ctrl_arm[7]+ctrl_ee[1]=8). Previous '14' came from github.com/robopen/roboagent/train.py's hardcoded state_dim=14, but that is a stale ALOHA/bimanual-derived config constant: detr_vae.py in the same repo builds input_proj_robot_state = nn.Linear(7, hidden_dim) with comment '7 for qpos', and elsewhere overrides state_dim = 8 (#14 commented out) for the CNNMLP baseline -- neither matches 14.; action_dim=arXiv:2309.01918 Appendix B.1 ('action space dimension of 8'); consistent with github.com/robopen/roboagent/blob/main/utils.py, which builds the action vector as np.concatenate([trial['data']['ctrl_arm'], trial['data']['ctrl_ee']]).; fps=arXiv:2309.01918 Appendix A: 'data was collected using an Oculus Quest 2 controller ... at 5Hz'; Appendix B.1: 'The robot is operated at a frequency of 5Hz.'; fps_variable=arXiv:2309.01918 states a single fixed control/collection frequency of 5Hz, with no mention of variable-rate recording.; num_camera_views=robopen.github.io/roboset/ 'We collected the dataset with 4 distinct camera views per frame'; arXiv:2309.01918 Section 4: 'The four Realsense D455 camera views provide complementary perspectives of the workspace'.; camera_views=Re-verified: robopen.github.io/roboset/ Data Schema image lists rgb_left, rgb_right, rgb_top, rgb_wrist (and matching d_* depth channels); arXiv:2309.01918 Sec.4/App.A confirm top+left+right fixed cameras plus a wrist camera. schema.py now defines a 'wrist' CameraView enum value, so the wrist camera is now represented directly instead of via suggested_new_enum_values; left/right map to 'side', top to 'top'.; depth_coverage=arXiv:2309.01918 Appendix A: 'MT-ACT dataset consisted of RGB and depth frames from four camera views'; cameras are Realsense D455 RGB-D sensors, so depth is available for all views.; has_language_instruction=robopen.github.io/roboset/teleoperation.html: 'Since each task is defined through a language instruction, there could be opportunities for language guided sequencing'; arXiv:2309.01918 uses a language-conditioned policy (MT-ACT) trained on per-task language embeddings.; num_task_types=robopen.github.io/roboset/teleoperation.html: 'We have a total of 12 skills, adequately represented across 38 tasks'; arXiv:2309.01918 abstract: 'demonstrate its generalization over 38 tasks'.; urdf_available=github.com/frankarobotics/franka_ros (official 'ROS integration for Franka research robots' repo) ships the franka_description package containing the manufacturer's URDF/xacro model for the Franka Panda arm used in RoboSet.; urdf_source=github.com/frankarobotics/franka_ros is maintained by Franka Robotics (the manufacturer), so the URDF is manufacturer-official rather than a community or dataset-repo reproduction.; expected_num_episodes=Re-verified 30050: robopen.github.io/roboset/teleoperation.html states 'Overall we have 30,050 trajectories ... 9,500 are collected through teleoperation'; arXiv:2309.01918 footnote 3 corroborates with '9,500 teleoperated ... 20,500 kinesthetic' (~30,000). Note: robopen.github.io/roboset/ (homepage) inconsistently states '28,500' trajectories (9,500 teleop + 19,000 kinesthetic) -- an apparent stale figure on that page; 30,050 is used as it is corroborated by both the teleoperation subpage and the paper's footnote arithmetic.; additional_modalities=robopen.github.io/roboset/ Data Schema image: tau_arm float[7] 'measured torque of arm joints' is recorded per trial -> force_torque modality confirmed. No tactile, audio, or eye_gaze fields appear in the schema or in arXiv:2309.01918.; paper_url=RoboAgent/MT-ACT paper describing RoboSet collection: arXiv:2309.01918 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.01918).; is_multi_embodiment=arXiv:2309.01918 and robopen.github.io/roboset/ describe a single Franka Emika Panda + Robotiq gripper embodiment throughout the core teleop+kinesthetic RoboSet; only a separate autonomous bin-picking release (excluded from this config's counts) uses an alternate D'Manus dexterous-hand end-effector on some subsets.; has_synchronized_multiview_rig=robopen.github.io/roboset/ Data Schema image groups rgb_left/right/top/wrist and d_left/right/top/wrist under a single 'data' record keyed by one shared 'time' field per trial step; robopen.github.io/roboset/teleoperation.html states 'four distinct camera views per frame', i.e. all 4 cameras are captured together at each recorded timestep.; action_frame=Inferred: github.com/robopen/roboagent/blob/main/utils.py builds the action tensor directly from raw h5 ctrl_arm/ctrl_ee fields with no delta/differencing step, and arXiv:2309.01918 App.B.1 describes 'joint position control' (not delta control). Moderate confidence, not explicitly labeled 'absolute' in the source.; expected_duration_hours=Derived estimate, not directly stated: github.com/robopen/roboagent/blob/main/utils.py hardcodes a filter requiring trial['data']['time'].shape[0] == 42 (with a cutoff of 2), and arXiv:2309.01918 Appendix A separately describes trials via '...the time-steps (40 steps)', consistent with a ~42-raw-step / ~40-effective-step episode length. At fps=5Hz that is ~8.4s/episode; 30,050 episodes * 8.4s / 3600 ~= 70.1 hours. This assumes episode length is roughly uniform across the whole 30,050-trajectory corpus, which is not explicitly confirmed for the kinesthetic portion.; num_scenes=arXiv:2309.01918 Sec.4: 'We collect the overall dataset across four different physical setups' with different kitchen-like environments; robopen.github.io/roboset/teleoperation.html data table enumerates trajectories under Scene 1/2/3/4.; release_type=Re-verified: RoboSet is a fixed, pre-collected set of teleoperated + kinesthetic trajectories released for download (robopen.github.io/roboset/), not a generative framework, scene platform, or RL benchmark environment.
suggested_new_enum_values: collection_method=mixed/kinesthetic -- re-confirmed still needed: the core RoboSet blends teleop (9,500, Oculus Quest 2) with kinesthetic playback-into-rearranged-scene demonstrations (~20,500); a separate ~70,000-trajectory release adds autonomous_policy rollouts. 'kinesthetic' has no existing enum value, and no single value captures this teleop+kinesthetic blend.

name: RoboTwin
field_sources: source_url=HF dataset page (huggingface.co/datasets/TianxingChen/RoboTwin2.0, confirmed live via HF API, license:mit tag) is the pre-collected 100k-trajectory release; code/paper mirror is github.com/RoboTwin-Platform/RoboTwin; license=Re-verified: GitHub README.md License section ('released under the MIT license'); HF API https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/TianxingChen/RoboTwin2.0 returns tags:['license:mit'], cardData.license='mit'; raw_format=Re-verified via robotwin-platform.github.io/doc/usage/configurations.html Minimal Example section: "An episode's data will be stored in one HDF5 file"; collection_method=Re-verified: arXiv:2506.18088 abstract - 'expert data synthesis pipeline that leverages multimodal language models (MLLMs) and simulation-in-the-loop refinement to automatically generate task-level execution code', executed entirely in SAPIEN simulation; no teleoperation or real-robot collection involved; embodiment_class=Re-verified: arXiv:2506.18088 title 'Robust Bimanual Robotic Manipulation' and Fig.5 'Five RoboTwin 2.0 Embodiments' - all 5 supported platforms are dual-arm rigs (single-arm robots combined in pairs per docs configurations.html); robot_platform=Re-verified: robotwin-platform.github.io/doc/usage/configurations.html Task & Embodiment Settings table lists 'Available Embodiment: ur5-wsg, ARX-X5, franka-panda, piper, aloha-agilex (dual-arm)'; aloha-agilex is the flagship default used in the paper's main benchmark table (Aloha AgileX dual-arm embodiment). See is_multi_embodiment and suggested_new_enum_values for the other 4.; num_arms=Re-verified: all 5 embodiments are used as dual-arm pairs (either native dual-arm like Aloha-AgileX, or two single-arm robots combined per configurations.html embodiment field description); dof_per_arm=Re-verified via arXiv:2506.18088 full text (arxiv.org/html/2506.18088): 'lower-DoF platforms such as Aloha-AgileX, Piper, and ARX-X5 (6-DoF)' vs 'high-DoF arms such as Franka and UR5 (7-DoF)'; value here (6) is for the default Aloha-AgileX embodiment recorded in robot_platform; gripper_type=Re-verified: arXiv:2506.18088 Appendix E - 'multiple gripper types, including the Panda gripper and WSG gripper' (both parallel-jaw); Fig.6 grasp illustrations show parallel-jaw grasping for all embodiments; has_mobile_base=Re-verified: arXiv:2506.18088 Fig.5/6 and task descriptions show all 5 embodiments as stationary tabletop dual-arm rigs; no mobile base anywhere in paper or docs; action_space=Re-verified via robotwin-platform.github.io/doc/usage/configurations.html Data Type section: data_type.qpos (joint position) and data_type.endpose (end-effector pose + gripper opening ratio) are both collected simultaneously in the released dataset's default configs (task_config/demo_clean.yml, demo_randomized.yml); action_frame=Re-verified: configurations.html Data Type / Note sections - qpos is absolute joint angles; endpose is 'end-effector pose in the world coordinate frame' (absolute, not delta); rotation_representation=Re-verified: configurations.html Note - endpose entries are 7-element lists 'following the order x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz' (quaternion); num_camera_views=Re-verified: configurations.html Camera Configuration section (collect_head_camera, collect_wrist_camera) and _base_task.py left_camera/right_camera/head_camera attributes -> 3 views (head + 2 wrists); camera_views=Re-verified: same as num_camera_views - head_camera (head), left_camera/right_camera (left_wrist/right_wrist) per _base_task.py and task_config/_camera_config.yml; has_camera_calibration=Re-verified: simulation environment (SAPIEN) - camera intrinsics/extrinsics for head/wrist cameras are exactly defined in task_config/_camera_config.yml (fovy, resolution) rather than estimated; depth_coverage=Re-verified against both official default task configs used to produce the released dataset: raw.githubusercontent.com/RoboTwin-Platform/RoboTwin/main/task_config/demo_clean.yml AND demo_randomized.yml both set data_type.depth: false, despite D435 cameras being depth-capable; depth is an opt-in data_type flag not enabled in either standard collection config; has_language_instruction=Re-verified: configurations.html language_num config field ('number of language descriptions to sample for each task'); arXiv:2506.18088 describes MLLM-generated diverse per-trajectory language instructions and a combinatorial augmentation pipeline (Appendix H/I); num_task_types=Re-verified: arXiv:2506.18088 abstract 'instantiated across 50 dual-arm tasks'; robotwin-platform.github.io/doc/tasks/index.html lists the 50 named tasks (confirmed via docs page table of contents); urdf_available=Re-verified: GitHub README Install & Download step downloads assets/embodiments/<name>/ meshes/config for simulation; expected_size_gb=Re-verified live: huggingface.co/datasets/TianxingChen/RoboTwin2.0/tree/main/dataset folder size badge reads '1.36 TB' (fetched directly, matches prior value of 1360.0 GB); expected_num_episodes=Re-verified: arXiv:2506.18088 abstract/Section 3.2 and GitHub README 'We provide over 100,000 pre-collected trajectories as part of the open-source release'; name: RoboVerse
field_sources: source_url=Official project homepage https://roboverseorg.github.io ('RoboVerse: Towards a Unified Platform, Dataset and Benchmark...'); cross-checked against GitHub org github.com/RoboVerseOrg/RoboVerse and roboverse.wiki. Re-confirmed unchanged.; paper_url=arXiv:2504.18904 'RoboVerse: Towards a Unified Platform, Dataset and Benchmark for Scalable and Generalizable Robot Learning' -- newly added; HF dataset card also tags arxiv:2504.18904.; license=Re-confirmed via GitHub API repos/RoboVerseOrg/RoboVerse -> license.spdx_id='Apache-2.0', and HF API datasets/RoboVerseOrg/roboverse_data -> tags include 'license:apache-2.0'. Note: bundled third-party robot/scene assets under robots/*, scenes/*/ carry their own separate LICENSE files that may differ from the Apache-2.0 code/dataset license.; raw_format=Re-confirmed via HF API file listing: trajectories stored as Python pickle (.pkl/.pkl.gz) files plus per-task initial_state_v2.json and .npy annotation arrays -- bespoke format, not RLDS/HDF5/LeRobot.; release_type=CORRECTED from fixed_episode_dataset to generation_framework. arXiv:2504.18904 abstract self-describes RoboVerse as 'a comprehensive framework comprising a simulation platform, a synthetic dataset, and unified benchmarks' built around MetaSim, a cross-simulator infrastructure for migrating/generating trajectories via motion planning, RL rollout, teleoperation, and generative task creation (Sec III, IV-A-C); the 510.5k-trajectory HF release is an evolving snapshot ('we will continue to maintain and expand it'), not a closed fixed collection. See suggested_new_enum_values for caveat.; collection_method=arXiv:2504.18904 Sec IV-B/IV-C: trajectories obtained via direct migration from existing sim benchmarks, motion planning + RL rollout, teleoperation, and generative task creation, all performed inside simulators -- overarching method is simulation. Re-confirmed unchanged.; secondary_collection_methods=arXiv:2504.18904 Sec IV-C: 'Teleoperation System for Trajectory Collection' via keyboard/phone/mocap/VR (-> teleop); 'Motion Planning and RL Rollout' used to generate complete trajectories from partial data (-> autonomous_policy); Sec XIV 'Real2Sim Toolset for Asset and Task Generation' reconstructs real-world objects/scenes into sim assets via Gaussian splatting/mesh reconstruction (-> scene_asset_curation).; is_multi_embodiment=Newly filled true. Same Table I evidence as embodiment_class plus Sec IV-E1: manipulation dataset (single-arm, dominant) coexists with a bimanual dexterous ShadowHand subset (trajs/bidex/), a Navigation dataset (Unitree Dog + JetBot, mobile), and a Humanoid dataset (Unitree H1 + dual Shadow Hands, HumanoidBench/Humanoid-X/SkillBlender) -- genuinely multi-embodiment at the platform level.; embodiment_class=arXiv:2504.18904 Table I: 276 task categories / 510.5k trajectories / 5.5k assets sourced from 15 tabletop manipulation benchmarks (ManiSkill, RLBench, CALVIN, Meta-World, RoboSuite/MimicGen, GAPartNet, Open6DOR, ARNOLD, LIBERO, Simpler, RLAfford, GraspNet, GarmentLab, UniDoorManip, GAPartManip), all single fixed-base-arm -- dominant/majority mode (~94% of released manipulation trajectories) recorded here; platform is multi-embodiment overall (see is_multi_embodiment).; num_arms=Same Table I evidence: dominant single-arm manipulation subset (510.5k trajectories) uses exactly one manipulator arm; smaller bidex bimanual subset uses two. Re-confirmed unchanged.; dof_per_hand=Newly filled. The bidex subset (trajs/bidex/ShadowHand* in HF dataset repo, per raw_format evidence) uses the Shadow Dexterous Hand. Shadow Robot Company official spec (shadowrobot.com/dexterous-hand-series) and Wikipedia 'Shadow Dexterous Hand': 24 total joints, 20 actuated degrees of freedom (4 further under-actuated movements). Recorded as the dominant/documented dexterous-hand platform in RoboVerse's bidex subset; not derived from the RoboVerse paper itself.; gripper_type=Same Table I source benchmarks predominantly use parallel two-finger grippers (Franka/Sawyer/UR5-class parallel grippers) -- dominant mode. bidex ShadowHand subset and h1_hand/shadow_hand/unitree_dex3-1 robot assets use dexterous_hand end-effectors instead; parallel_jaw recorded as dominant/majority mode only. Re-confirmed unchanged.; hand_pose_representation=Newly filled joint_angles (with caveat). Not explicitly stated per-bidex-subset in the paper; inferred from (1) arXiv:2504.18904 Sec XI-N/general trajectory format description that 'DoF position information of objects and robots is recorded in the trajectories', and (2) RoboVerse's entire pipeline represents robot state via URDF/MJCF joint hierarchies (Sec IX-X asset conversion), including the ShadowHand assets shipped as URDF/MJCF in the dataset repo -- no MANO mesh or 3D-keypoint hand representation found anywhere in the paper or repo.; has_mobile_base=Newly filled false, dominant-mode only (mirrors embodiment_class convention): manipulation dataset (510.5k trajectories, Table I) uses fixed-base tabletop arms. The separate Navigation dataset (Unitree Dog, JetBot) and Humanoid dataset (Unitree H1) do use mobile/legged bases, but are excluded from the dominant-mode figure per the same convention used for embodiment_class/gripper_type.; action_space=arXiv:2504.18904 Sec VI-E/App XIX-C: 'action conditions (gripper states with either Cartesian position plus orientation or joint position)' -- confirms both eef_pose and joint_position representations are used, matching 'mixed'. Re-confirmed unchanged.; action_frame=Newly filled both. arXiv:2504.18904 Sec VI-B-2 Implementation Details: 'the action is pre-processed into delta end-effector position space from absolute end-effector position space' -- raw eef actions stored in absolute frame, delta derived for generalist-model (OpenVLA/Octo) training; both frames coexist in the dataset ecosystem, analogous to the existing 'mixed' action_space heterogeneity.; has_camera_calibration=RoboVerse cameras are synthetic and fully specified via MetaSim's declarative config system (roboverse.wiki/metasim -- 'Configure Declaratively: Define robots, scenes, cameras...'), so intrinsics/extrinsics are exactly known by construction. Re-confirmed unchanged.; additional_modalities=Investigated, left blank. arXiv:2504.18904 Table VI (Sec VIII 'Simulators Overview') lists RGBD/Force/Contact/Tactile/IMU sensor CAPABILITIES of the underlying simulator engines (SAPIEN, PyBullet, MuJoCo, Genesis, etc.), but no statement found that RoboVerse's released HF trajectory files (trajs/*.pkl) actually persist force-torque, tactile, audio, or eye-gaze channels -- Table VI describes engine capability, not confirmed recorded modalities, so left blank rather than inferred.; has_language_instruction=arXiv:2504.18904: many migrated benchmarks carry per-task language instructions (Sec IV Navigation 'off-the-shelf instructions from R2R/RxR'; AI-assisted task generation gives 'a short, human-readable instruction'; GraspNet subset has 'diverse and challenging language instructions'). Re-confirmed unchanged.; urdf_available=Re-confirmed via HF API file listing: 177 .urdf files plus MJCF/USD robot descriptions under robots/ (franka/, Kinova_Gen3/, Interbotix_WidowX_250/, h1_hand/, unitree_dex3-1/, etc).; urdf_source=Same HF dataset repo (RoboVerseOrg/roboverse_data) ships URDF/MJCF/USD files directly under robots/ within its own repo, each with a bundled LICENSE file -- dataset_repo. Re-confirmed unchanged.; num_task_types=arXiv:2504.18904 Table I total row: '276 510.5k 5.5k' (task categories, trajectories, assets) across migrated manipulation benchmarks; excludes the separate Navigation (VLN-CE) and Humanoid datasets. Re-confirmed unchanged.; expected_size_gb=HF Hub API datasets/RoboVerseOrg/roboverse_data?expand=usedStorage reports usedStorage = 44869086705 bytes (~44.9 GB) as of re-check (repo lastModified 2026-06-08). Re-confirmed unchanged.; expected_num_episodes=arXiv:2504.18904 Table I total row and Sec IV-E1: 'this migration results in 276 task categories, 510.5k trajectories, and 5.5k assets' for the manipulation dataset; excludes Navigation (30k episodes) and Humanoid datasets. Re-confirmed unchanged.; num_objects=Newly filled 5500 (~5.5k). arXiv:2504.18904 Table I total row: '# Assets' column sums to 5.5k across the 15 migrated manipulation benchmarks. Caveat: 'assets' as tabulated may include some non-graspable scene/articulated-furniture props alongside pure manipulable objects, so this is the closest available proxy for num_objects, not a strictly object-only count.
suggested_new_enum_values: robot_platform=multi_platform -- HF dataset repo's robots/ directory ships dozens of distinct robot descriptions (Franka, Kinova Gen3, Interbotix WidowX 250, KUKA LBR IIWA14, ARX L5, UFactory Lite6, Unitree Z1, UR5e/UR10e, Siasun SO-ARM100, Unitree H1, Shadow Hand, Unitree Dex3-1, etc.) migrated from 15+ source benchmarks; no single enum value or 'other' can honestly represent this, so left blank.; rotation_representation=mixed -- source benchmarks migrated into RoboVerse (RLBench, CALVIN, LIBERO, ManiSkill, Meta-World, etc.) each natively use different orientation encodings (quaternion/euler/rotation matrix depending on origin simulator); no single dataset-wide value confirmed. A 'mixed' option analogous to the existing action_space 'mixed' value would let this be recorded honestly instead of left blank.; release_type=hybrid_platform_dataset_benchmark -- RoboVerse is simultaneously (1) a cross-simulator generation framework (MetaSim), (2) a static ~510.5k-trajectory dataset snapshot released on HuggingFace, and (3) a unified IL+RL benchmark suite (Sec V). None of the four current release_type values individually captures all three; generation_framework was chosen as the closest single fit since the framework/unification aspect is the paper's core contribution, but a hybrid label would be more precise for platforms like this.

name: RT-1

fps=arXiv:2212.06817 Sec 4: 'RT-1 performs closed-loop control and commands actions at 3 Hz'.; fps_variable=Paper describes a single fixed 3 Hz control rate with no mention of variable rate; also a fixed-time waiting mechanism is used to avoid jitter (App C.1).; collection_method=arXiv:2110.00534 Sec 3.2: two vetted crowdworkers are live-paired per session as Commander/Follower; the Follower's navigation and object-interaction actions are chosen by the human annotator in real time, i.e. teleoperation of the simulated embodiment; secondary_collection_methods=arXiv:2110.00534 Sec 3.2: sessions are collected entirely inside the AI2-THOR simulator (Kolve et al. 2017); is_multi_embodiment=arXiv:2110.00534 Sec 3.2: only the Follower embodiment executes environment actions; robot_platform=Simulated AI2-THOR agent (Kolve et al. 2017 AI2-THOR paper cited in TEACh); not a named commercial robot platform, so classified as 'other'; gripper_type=arXiv:2110.00534 Sec 3.1: object interaction is abstracted to an action id plus a relative image coordinate (e.g. Pickup, Place); fps_variable=Simulation advances one discrete step per issued action (event-driven action stepping via AI2-THOR, not sampling at a fixed control rate); github.com/alexa/teach teach_replay writes one frame per action step, not per fixed time interval; num_camera_views=github.com/alexa/teach README 'Replaying episodes': teach_replay 'save[s] egocentric observations of the Commander and Driver [Follower]' at each timestep -> 2 first-person view streams; camera_views=github.com/alexa/teach README + arXiv:2110.00534 Fig.1/Fig.2: Follower view is a first-person, head-height egocentric view (head); Commander view is a free-floating/disembodied search camera not attached to any body (other); has_synchronized_multiview_rig=Simulated environment (AI2-THOR); the two view streams are separate simulated camera feeds, not a physical synchronized multi-camera rig; has_camera_calibration=No camera calibration files are distributed in github.com/alexa/teach; num_scenes=arXiv:2110.00534 Table 2, 'TEACh Overall' row: Unique Scenes = 109 distinct AI2-THOR floor plans (kitchens, living rooms, bedrooms, bathrooms) used across the released sessions
suggested_new_enum_values: license=CDLA-Sharing-1.0 -- per github.com/alexa/teach license files (DATALICENSE), all non-image data files (game sessions, EDH/TfD instances, annotations) are released under Community Data License Agreement - Sharing v1.0; images are separately licensed Apache-2.0 (IMAGESLICENSE) and code under MIT (SOFTWARELICENSE).
